title: What we know so far about the plane crash that killed 11 European tourists near one of Peru’s most popular sites
description: Peru has temporarily suspended the operations of sightseeing airline Aerodiana after one of its planes crashed in the country’s Ica region on Saturday, killing 11 European tourists and two crew member...
fullText:
Peru has temporarily suspended the operations of sightseeing airline Aerodiana after one of its planes crashed in the country's Ica region on Saturday, killing 11 European tourists and two crew members.

Aerodiana, which flies customers over the Nazca Lines archaeological site in southern Peru, must suspend all operations "until investigations are completed to verify the company's compliance with the applicable aviation regulations, procedures and operating requirements," Peru's Ministry of Transportation and Communications said Sunday.

CNN has reached out to Aerodiana for comment.

The Peruvian government earlier said that the crew of the small sightseeing plane had reported a mechanical problem before radio contact was lost.

"There was a call from the aircraft indicating that it was experiencing mechanical problems," Peruvian Foreign Trade and Tourism Minister Rogers Valencia told reporters at the crash site near the Nazca Lines, a collection of ancient geoglyphs etched into the desert floor.

The UNESCO world heritage site features designs of animals and geometric shapes that are best seen from the air. The flight was taking tourists to view the desert markings.

The ministry earlier said the pilots of the Cessna 208B Grand Caravan, which can carry 12 passengers, notified the control tower at Nazca airfield of the emergency, in the aircraft's final radio transmission.

Valencia said the Aviation Accident Investigation Commission is analyzing the call, the plane's flight path, along with mechanical evidence from the wreckage, but authorities have not said whether the reported problem caused the crash.

Those aboard included 11 tourists from Spain, Italy and Germany, as well as the two Peruvian crew members.

"There will be immediate results, and the process of assessing the condition of the wreckage will provide an in-depth understanding of the cause" of the accident, Valencia added.

Valencia said the Italian and German consuls were at the scene and he offered his condolences over the deaths of seven Italian and two German tourists. Two Spanish tourists also died, according to official information.

The Italian Foreign Ministry said its embassy in Lima was in contact with Peruvian authorities and that the families of the Italian victims have already been notified. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on X: "On behalf of the Italian government and on my own behalf, I express my deepest condolences to their loved ones at this time of immense grief."

Valencia said Pisco Airport, from where the Aerodiana flight took off, is "fully operational" and that "we need to determine the extent of liability" in the crash.

Asked about a possible suspension of operations at Pisco Airport, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori told reporters that "the suspension of the airport is being evaluated," but added that she wanted to wait until the investigation was complete and ministers had submitted their reports.

In a statement issued before its operations were suspended, Aerodiana said it extended its condolences to the victims' families and is "fully prepared to provide the necessary support."

"Throughout our 18 years of operation, we have maintained an unwavering commitment to the safety of our passengers and crews. Therefore, this incident affects us deeply and reaffirms our willingness to cooperate with full accountability in whatever is required by the authorities," the airline said.

According to the ministry, the accident occurred around 1 p.m. local time (2 p.m. ET), about 2 kilometers (1.2 miles) from Nazca airfield, after the plane took off from Pisco Airport for a flight over the Nazca Lines.

There have been other deadly crashes involving sightseeing flights near the Nazca Lines. In 2022, five tourists and two Peruvian crew members died when an aircraft went down near the site, Reuters reported. And in a 2010 accident, four British tourists and two Peruvian crew members were killed when their light aircraft crashed.

CNN'S Mauricio Torres contributed to this report. With information from Spanish international news agency EFE.

title: Ukraine hopes to coax back thousands of AWOL troops with their choice of commander and deployment area
description: Kyiv says troops can use a mobile app to skip much of the return process and deploy immediately to their new, preferred unit.
fullText:
Ukraine's return program says it's letting AWOL troops choose from over 70 units for redeployment.

The missing soldiers can indicate their preferences for where they want to serve and in what roles.

It's an attempt to solve the hundreds of thousands of AWOL cases it's suffered since the war began.

Ukraine is giving its missing troops a bonus for rejoining the war: The chance to choose their new area of deployment, commander, and job.

Kyiv's defense ministry said on Friday that it would allow troops who are absent without leave, or AWOL, to choose from over 70 units across its three ground branches if they redeploy.

The announcement is an expansion of a voluntary return program, launched in June, that aims to coax tens of thousands of AWOL troops back within 100 days. That's a priority for Ukraine, which has struggled to keep its ranks filled for years, reinforcing a vicious cycle where its remaining, outnumbered troops grow increasingly fatigued.

The program "allows you to choose a new military unit from a specified list, indicate your desired direction of service and previous experience, receive support from the contact center, and arrive immediately at the new unit," the ministry said in its Friday announcement.

Troops have until September 20 to apply for their return, it added.

Social media has made it common for Ukrainian commanders and units to have their own reputations for the survival rate and welfare of their troops. That's made some units far more popular than others.

Still, the defense ministry appeared to add a caveat — there's no guarantee a soldier will get their preferred unit or role.

"At the same time, the number of positions in individual areas is limited, so those who have already decided on a unit, area of service, and desired position should not delay submitting a report," its statement said.

But the ministry has repeatedly sought this year to assure soldiers that its new systems are designed with common sense, not bureaucracy, in mind, preventing troops from falling through the cracks.

"Drivers, UAV operators, clerks, shooters — the army needs everyone," said Mstislav Banik, deputy minister for defense.

Led until recently by the maverick Mykhailo Fedorov, the ministry has tried to radically modernize its military's structure and retain troops.

Previously, an AWOL soldier had to report to the military law enforcement service to officially register their absence, which is punishable by up to 10 years in prison. They would have then been sent to a reserve battalion, where they could be redeployed to their new unit.

But the new program skips all of that, the ministry said, instead sending troops directly to their preferred unit. Once there, they'll be blocked from involuntary transfer to another unit for six months.

Instead of reporting to the military police, the AWOL troops can apply to rejoin the war via a website or Ukraine's military mobile app, Army+, officials added.

Fedorov said in January that Ukraine had logged over 200,000 AWOL cases since the war began. That figure may, however, be significantly inflated by an administrative loophole that allowed disgruntled troops to dodge the red tape of transferring units by going AWOL.

Ukraine also recently raised troop salary ceilings dramatically, with assault soldiers able to earn over six figures a year depending on how frequently they fought.

fullText:
NEW YORK, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Kay Granger, a Texas Republican who was the first woman from her party ‌to chair the U.S. House of Representatives' powerful Appropriations ‌Committee, has died, her son J.D. Granger confirmed to Reuters on Sunday. ​She was 83.

No cause of death was given. Kay Granger in 2024 said she was battling "unforeseen health challenges."

Granger represented her Texas district in Congress from 1997 to 2025. In 2023, Granger announced ‌she would not seek ⁠re-election to the U.S. House of Representatives.

In her final term as a lawmaker, Granger chaired the ⁠House Appropriations Committee for more than a year, putting her in charge of spending legislation and making her one of the ​most influential ​members of Congress.

House Speaker Mike ​Johnson praised Granger as a ‌trailblazer. "Throughout her career, she broke barriers for women in public service," Johnson said, noting that she was the first female mayor of Fort Worth and the first Republican woman elected to represent Texas in the U.S. House.

She was the first Republican ‌woman to lead the budget panel, ​although two Democratic women, Representatives Nita ​Lowey and Rosa DeLauro, ​preceded Granger in the role.

"At every step of ‌her career, she [Granger] earned the ​respect of Members ​on both sides of the aisle through her steady leadership and deep belief in the importance of Congress fulfilling ​its constitutional responsibility ‌to invest in the American people," DeLauro said in ​a statement on Sunday.

title: Firstmate: Talk to one agent. Ship with a crew
description: Talk to one agent. Ship with a crew. Contribute to kunchenguid/firstmate development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
You can run one coding agent easily.
But the moment you want three project tasks done in parallel - fixes, investigations, plans, audits - you become a tab-juggler: babysitting sessions, copy-pasting context between repos, forgetting which terminal had the failing test.

firstmate flips the model.
You talk to a single agent - the first mate - and it runs the crew for you: spawning autonomous agents in a visible session backend, giving each a clean git worktree, supervising them to completion, and handing you finished PRs, approved local merges, or standalone investigation reports.
For larger fleets, you can opt in to persistent secondmates: second mates that are still ordinary direct reports, but run from their own isolated firstmate homes.

firstmate is not a model, not a harness, not a skill, not an MCP server, and not a CLI.
firstmate is an agent distro for running a crew of agents.
An agent distro is a portable directory of instructions, skills, tooling, policies, and state conventions that turns a general-purpose agent into a specialized one.
There is no app to install: the cloned repo is the distro - AGENTS.md, bundled firstmate skills, and helper scripts that any terminal coding agent can follow.
Launching a supported harness inside it instantiates your first mate - and makes you the captain.

All three have verified turn-end guard paths when launched with their documented setup.
Pick whichever one matches your subscription and workflow.

The hidden operational inputs remain ordinary user-role messages with unchanged delivery, ordering, authority, persistence, and exports.
The preference persists for the effective Firstmate home, and toggling it off restores ordinary rendering.
Calm's current behavior and supported limits are separate from its version-scoped maintainer evidence.

Setup guides for tmux (the default) and every other supported backend (herdr, zellij, Orca, cmux) are linked in Documentation below.

You chat with the first mate.
It routes each request to a crewmate in its own session endpoint and git worktree, supervises the fleet with a zero-token event-driven watcher, and brings you finished PRs, approved local merges, or investigation reports.
Optional secondmates extend this to persistent second mates, dispatch profiles let you steer which harness handles which task, and an opt-in X mode lets the same fleet answer public mentions.
codex-app is not a runtime backend yet; docs/codex-app-backend.md owns the Codex App boundary.

Full architecture - the supervision engine, worktree isolation, secondmates, dispatch profiles, project modes, optional X mode, fleet sync, and self-update - is in docs/architecture.md.

title: OpenUK Wants Britain to Stop Giving Away Open Source Creations
description: They point to MCP, built by two engineers in London, that ended up under US-based governance.
fullText:
OpenUK recently published its AI Openness report, and buried inside the 40-page document is a big ask from the UK government. Build Britain its own foundation that holds code, governance, and standards the way the Linux Foundation (LF) does in the US.

If you are hearing that name for the first time, OpenUK is a UK-based (obviously) non-profit that advocates for open technology and is led by Amanda Brock. They first put out this call in a report titled "Making the UK the Home of Open Source," which was submitted to UKRI earlier this year.

The AI Openness report restates the case with added urgency this time.

Characterizing the proposed British flavor of LF as a National Foundation, the body, once formed, would hold repositories, standards, and datasets built with UK public money rather than watch that work migrate to servers and governance boards based elsewhere.

It would also handle training, community engagement, and event organizing. Those are areas that would otherwise need separate infrastructure, like an open source program office (OSPO) and a sovereign fund.

OpenUK frames this as a funding and governance gap more than a technology one.

They note that the UK ranks as Europe's top country in open source software and AI openness, yet it has no equivalent to the Linux Foundation, Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency, or China's Open Atom Foundation to show for it.

The non-profit didn't have to look far to prove its point, as MCP is the group's strongest example.

The Model Context Protocol, now the standard behind how AI models connect to outside tools and data, was created by two engineers in London. Anthropic backed the protocol and eventually donated it to LF's Agentic AI Foundation, alongside Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification.

In conversation with OpenUK, David Soria Parra, one of MCP's co-creators, said that they gave MCP away because they needed the standard to stay vendor neutral, free of trademark and licensing risk.

If the UK had an established foundation, then they wouldn't have lost MCP to the US. 🙃

The European Commission has already shown off an initiative to break free from US tech dominance by moving towards an open European digital ecosystem. It would cover fields like cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, open hardware, internet technologies, and industrial applications like automotive and manufacturing.

Germany is closer to what OpenUK wants for the UK. Its Sovereign Tech Fund has turned into a government agency, and the report calls that "the right direction."

China has already proven the model works. Open source became a national pillar under its 14th Five-Year Plan, supported by a dedicated foundation called the Open Atom Foundation.

DeepSeek’s R1 showed how that focus pays off, leveraging open-weights and knowledge distillation to deliver frontier-level AI at a fraction of the cost.

OpenUK looks to garner interest from various public sector organizations across the UK while also aiming to collaborate with global experts, delivering the best proposal for their country as a result.

title: Your Coding Agent Is Playing Tetris Badly
description:
Say you're playing Tetris. You're not careful, and you leave a hole. Now that row won't clear. What do you do?
Some players will try their hardest to dig it out.
fullText:
Say you’re playing Tetris. You’re not careful, and you leave a hole. Now that row won’t clear. What do you do?

Some players will try their hardest to dig it out. Some players will ignore it and keep dropping blocks, since the stack isn’t tall enough to bother them. The hole is tech debt.

Coding agents tend to belong to the second group. When faced with problems, they prioritize adding code, not removing it. Sometimes they’ll reimplement the same thing 3 times over. Because they don’t know it already exists. Because their context window only lets them see a few rows at a time.

This is mostly fine when your app has a small scope. Your stack is low. The app still works. The game is still playable with all these holes.

But as your app gets more complicated, when you’re asking the agent to add the 20th feature instead of the 3rd, it gets very hard for the agent to fix old bugs without introducing new ones. You only have a bit of space on top now. Every block becomes dangerous and requires gymnastics to place, because you don’t have a strong foundation.

Is it possible to get your coding agent to plug the holes early? Maybe. But you have to recognize the issue and spell out exactly how to refactor (most vibe coders don’t). Without that, agents are really bad at refactoring, because they’re really good at justifying the existence of every line of code.

Somewhere along the way people forgot that the point of Tetris is to keep the stack low. Now it’s all about how fast you can drop blocks. They look at the tower and marvel. Look how many features we’ve shipped! Then one day the bugs stop being fixable. Game over.

title: Gnt, a company brain AI agents check before acting
description: git-native rules layer for AI agents. Every rule is a file, reviewed and merged like code - gnt-ai/gnt
fullText:
Run the setup below once and every agent your team runs has a git-native rulebook it has to check over MCP before it acts, approved the same way your code already is: a merged pull request.

Prefer not to run any of this yourself? The hosted version at gntai.dev does the same thing without you standing up a Postgres instance.

gnt prebrain scanning a repo, opening a PR, and getting it merged. A real terminal session, not a mockup.

That merge lands a rule file in your connected repo, shaped like this:

Each file is plain markdown with YAML frontmatter:

There's no captured transcript to show yet (see the gap noted at the bottom of this README).
Here's the actual response shape a check_action call returns, straight from the tool's
contract:

verdict is one of allowed, blocked, or needs_human. needs_human is the fail-closed
default: no approved rule covers the action, retrieval failed, or the check couldn't complete.
It never guesses.

gnt needs Node >=22.13. If the CLI fails to start with a version error, update Node first and confirm with node --version.

Self-hosting: gnt login's browser step has nowhere to land. gnt login opens a browser to a /cli-login page and polls the API for the resulting key — that page is served by the hosted product's web app, which isn't part of this repo. There's no CLI-only login flow (device code or otherwise) today, and no gnt command to set a key manually. Self-hosting this stack currently means building your own thin frontend for that one route (it just needs to complete the sign-in flow and hand the CLI a key). This is a real, open gap in the self-host path, not a config issue — closing it properly means adding a CLI-only login flow.

ValueError: refusing to start: these settings still have their .env.example placeholder value... A change-me-... string is still sitting in apps/api/.env. The error names every offending field; generate a real value for each and retry.

store fails to start with GNT_STORE_INTERNAL_API_SECRET is not set. apps/store/.env wasn't filled in, or wasn't picked up. Confirm the file exists at that exact path, not still named .env.example.

Every store-to-api call gets rejected with 401 or 403, even though both services are up. STORE_INTERNAL_API_SECRET / APPROVAL_SIGNING_SECRET in apps/api/.env don't byte-for-byte match GNT_STORE_INTERNAL_API_SECRET / GNT_APPROVAL_SIGNING_SECRET in apps/store/.env. This fails closed by design. Regenerate both pairs so the two files agree.

A rule fails to save with an embedding or rerank error. apps/store/.env is missing ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY, or it's still empty. Get a real one from zeroentropy.dev.

Self-hosting gnt costs you nothing, forever — clone it, run docker compose up, bring your own keys. What we sell is the part self-hosting doesn't give you: hosting at gntai.dev, managed OAuth connectors (GitHub, Slack, Linear, Notion, Zendesk — no app-approval process on your end), and usage-based AI features. If you'd rather run it yourself, that's a fully supported, fully free path, not a crippled trial of the real thing.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for dev setup and how to open a PR. Every commit needs a Signed-off-by trailer (git commit -s), the Developer Certificate of Origin instead of a CLA. No separate form, just the flag.

title: Eve Marketing Team Template
description: Team of marketing agents built on eve. Contribute to vercel-labs/marketing-team-eve-template development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Team of marketing agents built on eve. You bring work to a team lead: a launch to plan,posts to write, or a page that isn't converting. The lead holds the shared picture of the product, routes the request to the specialist who does that kind of work, and hands back what they produced.

The dependency runs one way. The product marketer writes the brand context; everyone else reads it at the start of every task. That makes it the one piece of shared state whose quality bounds everything else, which is why a single specialist owns authoring it.

The specialists do not overlap by accident. The product marketer decides what the team claims, the content marketer writes the words, seo decides which pages should exist, and social-media-coordinator and email are the two that can put something in front of an audience.

A newsletter is the case where two specialists chain. The content marketer authors the prose; the email specialist reworks it for the inbox and runs Resend.

Splitting it this way keeps the newsletter inside the planning and editing passes the content marketer already runs, instead of growing a second, thinner writer.

Every irreversible action stops for an approve or deny decision, rendered as a button in Slack or the TUI.

The Resend connection goes one step further than gating. It narrows what the model can discover at all with tools.allow, cutting roughly 85 published tools to the 47 that make up the campaign, list, and diagnostic surface. Account administration such as API key creation and domain writes is never on the table.

Opening a fresh conversation with the team pins four starting prompts. Slack renders at most four, so it is one per specialist rather than a tour of the whole team.

Each one names the deliverable, asks for the brand context and your preferences, then hands the interview back, so an unspecified request costs one question rather than a wasted delegation.

This requires assistant:write under Bot Scopes and the assistant_thread_started and app_home_opened trigger event types. Without them the prompts never appear, and the rest of the channel is unaffected.

The deploy button helps you provision and wire up everything:

Then talk to the lead in the dev TUI or your own front end, and it routes work to the specialists.

Resend sending. Verify a sending domain and create at least one segment in the Resend dashboard. The agent reads that state and picks from it, but cannot create a domain or verify DNS for you. The Resend connector is user-scoped, so each person authorizes their own login the first time they ask for email work, and sends are attributed to whoever approved them. Skip if you are not using email.

Working in Claude Code or Cursor? Paste this:

Typefully's MCP server only accepts a static key, so it is the single credential in the project and its connection is shared across all users.

Resend is the one place per-user scoping earns its keep. Sending is the only thing this team does that cannot be undone, so a per-user token means the approval names who agreed to it and Resend records who sent it, instead of every campaign arriving from one shared workspace key.

Every specialist directory holds the same shape: an agent.ts with the routing description, an instructions.md, its own sandbox.ts, a tools/ with the five asset tools plus get_brand_context and the artifact tools, a bash.ts that disables the shell, and its own skills/.

Two specialists carry an evidence boundary worth knowing about. seo has no crawler, rank tracker, or Search Console, and its audit checklist marks every check as verifiable by fetch or not verifiable at all. email cannot see inbox placement or domain reputation, and its deliverability checklist does the same. Both are built to say what they could not check rather than infer it.

Link the project you deployed, or a fresh one, and pull its environment:

There is no unit test suite. Verify with pnpm validate, which must report 0 errors and 0 warnings, then exercise the agent in the TUI. Approval gates render there too, so it is the place to confirm a send actually stops before it goes out.

npx eve info is the fastest way to confirm a change landed. If a file you added does not appear, discovery did not classify it as an authored slot, and .eve/discovery/diagnostics.json says why.

The Deploy button does this for you. For a project you did not create with the button, use the Vercel CLI:

Verify a sending domain in the Resend dashboard as well. Nothing can be sent without one.

Where to edit, at a glance. CUSTOMIZING.md is the walkthrough, with recipes for adding a specialist, skill, tool, or connection, and the silent failures worth knowing about.

The agent auto-updates as you edit these files.

Specialists do not have to live in this repo. eve's remote agents let the lead delegate to an agent in its own deployment, with its own skills, connections, and release cycle. vercelOidc() handles deployment-to-deployment auth with no shared secret.

Set PAID_ADS_AGENT_URL, and the lead picks the specialist up from its description exactly as it does the local ones. The result comes back as a normal tool result. This suits work needing credentials or a release cycle you would rather keep out of this repo, such as ad platform access.

Deeper internals live in ARCHITECTURE.md, and conventions for working in this repo live in AGENTS.md.

title: Trail – signed OpenTelemetry spans for AI agents
description: Contribute to varmax2511/trail development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Signed OpenTelemetry GenAI spans for AI agents. Capture, normalize, verify — bring your own backend.

Trail is a Python SDK that captures what AI agents actually do — every LLM call, tool invocation, MCP call, and skill execution — as OpenTelemetry spans with a small Trail extension namespace. It signs each session with Ed25519 and exports via OTLP to any OTel backend (Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, Chronosphere, ...). Trail does not store, query, or dashboard. Storage and query are your existing backend's job.

When an agent misbehaves in production, three questions are surprisingly hard to answer:

Trail adds the three things that are missing: an agent-aware tool taxonomy (internal / mcp / skill / builtin), MCP injection flagging on tool responses, and a skill hash that detects silent substitution — all as standard OpenTelemetry spans, so any OTel backend ingests them with no translation layer.

Trail models an agent run as an OpenTelemetry span tree — one invoke_agent root span per session, with every LLM call, tool, MCP call, and skill nested underneath — and layers a trail.* attribute namespace on top. That structure, plus three purpose-built attributes, is what turns each question above into a query.

Which tool ran, in what order, with what inputs?
Every tool invocation becomes an execute_tool span tagged with gen_ai.tool.name and trail.tool_type (internal / mcp / skill / builtin) — the agent-shaped distinction a plain LLM tracer never draws. Order and nesting come from the OpenTelemetry SDK's contextvars propagation, which stays correct across async/await and concurrent asyncio tasks, so each span attaches to the right parent. Inputs and outputs are recorded as trail.input_hash / trail.output_hash (SHA-256, computed off the hot path) plus a sensitivity flag — tamper-evident identity of the payloads without storing the payloads themselves.

Was that MCP server response trying to inject instructions?
When Trail wraps an MCP call_tool, it runs the response through a YAML injection ruleset — instruction-override, system-prompt injection, role override, credential-exfil phrasing (override via TRAIL_MCP_RULES) — and stamps the span with trail.mcp.injection_flag. A response that says "ignore your previous instructions and…" lands as an ordinary span with trail.mcp.injection_flag = true, next to trail.mcp.server_id for provenance.

Is this skill the same code it was yesterday?
wrap_skill() records trail.skill.hash — a SHA-256 over the skill's source (trail.skill.hash_method = "source", with a qualname-fallback for C-extensions and lambdas). Same skill → same hash; a silent swap → a different hash on today's span versus yesterday's. Diff the attribute across two sessions and substitution is visible.

Then you ask where you already look. Trail only captures — the questions get answered in your backend. In dev mode that's the session JSONL (~/.trail/sessions/{trace_id}.jsonl), and trail verify-export proves none of it was altered after the fact (and pinpoints the span if it was). In prod, it's an ordinary attribute filter — trail.tool_type = "mcp" AND trail.mcp.injection_flag = true — in Grafana, Honeycomb, or Datadog.

That's it. By default Trail writes spans to ~/.trail/sessions/{trace_id}.jsonl and a short summary to stderr. Zero infrastructure.

To ship to your OTel backend instead:

Async OpenAI (AsyncOpenAI) is instrumented automatically by the same trail.auto_instrument() call.

Trail ships a trail-hook console script. Wire it into ~/.claude/settings.json. A single binary handles all three events — it reads the event name from Claude Code's stdin payload and dispatches internally.

Already have hooks? Claude Code's hooks.<EventName> is an array — Trail composes alongside whatever is already there. Append a new {matcher, hooks} block per event rather than replacing the array. Trail runs sequentially with your existing hooks and never blocks them (it exits 0 even on internal errors).

See it end to end: examples/demo_claude_code/run_demo.sh replays a real Claude Code session against trail-hook (no infrastructure, no API key) — captures the tool taxonomy, flags a prompt-injection riding in on an MCP-fetched GitHub issue, then verify-export proves the session and catches a tamper.

Every Claude Code tool call — including MCP calls and skills — is now captured. The SessionEnd hook is the moment the session gets its Merkle root + Ed25519 signature. (Signing is wired to SessionEnd, which fires once when the session terminates — not Stop, which fires at the end of every turn and would leave later turns' spans unsigned.)

Google's Agent Development Kit is OpenTelemetry-native, so Trail rides ADK's own
execute_tool spans rather than re-instrumenting — one auto_instrument() call
adds the tool taxonomy and MCP injection flag ADK doesn't produce, and wrapping
the run in trail.session() signs it.

Every ADK tool call now carries trail.tool_type (McpTool → mcp,
ADK-provided search/memory tools → builtin, your FunctionTools → internal)
and MCP responses are scanned for injection (trail.mcp.injection_flag).

Try it in dev mode first — zero infrastructure. Dev mode is the default, so
the two lines above already write every ADK span to
~/.trail/sessions/{trace_id}.jsonl locally (no network). Run your agent, then
inspect what was captured:

Signing is opt-in. With no keys present, sessions are simply unsigned —
the minimal setup: spans + trail.tool_type + MCP injection flag, no
tamper-evidence, no signing overhead. Turn it on when you want it:

Dev-mode note: don't also enable ADK's own Cloud Trace / OTel exporter
while running dev mode. Trail configures the tracer provider; if ADK sets one
first, Trail's local JSONL won't attach. Just add the two Trail lines and
leave ADK's own tracing off.

When it looks right locally, ship the same code to your backend — ADK exports
OTLP, so set TRAIL_EXPORT=otlp and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (e.g.
Chronosphere) and the spans flow there instead. See
docs/backends/chronosphere.md, and
examples/adk_manual_instrumentation.py
for the framework-agnostic manual path (no adapter required).

ADK has no first-class "skill", so skill-hashing stays with trail.wrap_skill,
which composes with ADK. Parallel/merged tool calls are a documented v1 gap.

Standard OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes:

Plus the Trail extension — the novel part:

In Grafana or Honeycomb, these render as ordinary GenAI spans. The trail.* attributes are queryable like any other attribute (trail.tool_type = "mcp" AND trail.mcp.injection_flag = true).

Trail emits spans only — no Prometheus scrape endpoint and no OTel metrics. To get rate / error / duration counters or a "MCP injections per minute" panel, drop the OpenTelemetry Collector's spanmetrics connector into your pipeline and label by trail.tool_type, trail.mcp.injection_flag, etc. Span backends (Tempo's metrics-generator, Datadog APM metrics, Honeycomb derived columns) offer equivalent backend-side derivations. Two signal types at the source would duplicate the signal — the Collector composes them cleanly.

Each session is signed once at session end with Ed25519 over a Merkle root of its span content. Anyone with the public key can verify it later — no Trail infrastructure required:

Modified spans, removed spans, and added spans are all detected by the Merkle root mismatch.

Per-backend setup (endpoint, auth, query examples) lives in
docs/backends/ — Grafana Tempo, Honeycomb, Datadog,
Chronosphere. For clusters, see docs/deployment/kubernetes.md.

In: OpenAI SDK adapter, Google ADK adapter, Claude Code hooks, OTel GenAI emission, tool taxonomy, MCP injection flagging, skill hash, session-checkpoint signing, OTLP transport, dev-mode JSONL, verify-export, generate-keys.

Not yet: LangChain / LlamaIndex / AutoGen adapters, HTTP proxy, sidecar deployment, CloudTrail / CloudWatch transports, encrypted sensitive-content side-store, GDPR erasure workflow, multi-org config, KMS-backed signing.

Suppression-resistant capture (HTTP proxy + sidecar), per-event / checkpoint signing for crash safety, additional framework adapters (LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen), encrypted sensitive-content side-store, GDPR erasure workflow, KMS-backed signing, additional transports (CloudTrail, CloudWatch).

See trail_hld.md for the high-level design and CLAUDE.md for implementation conventions.

Trail produces signed, tamper-evident telemetry — reports against the signing /
verification path are taken seriously. See SECURITY.md for the
disclosure process and what is in scope.

Apache-2.0. See LICENSE and NOTICE.

fullText:
The countdown to another high school football season is over.

Teams across the Miami Valley have preparations underway with the goal of winning conference championships and making postseason runs. It all will culminate with state championship weekend in early December in Canton.

From new coaches and rule changes to divisional shifts and must-see early-season matchups, there is plenty for fans to know before kickoff. Here are five things to know as the 2026 Ohio high school football season gets ready to begin.

The calendarThe 18-week journey from the start of camps to the state championship games will be filled with memorable moments as always.

It all starts with practices, which officially began Saturday, Aug. 1. The first set of scrimmages in the area begin Thursday, Aug. 6 and continue through Aug. 14.

The first Friday night of the season will be Aug. 21. A few games in the area will get underway the night before as well.

The 10-week regular season concludes the weekend of Oct. 23. The first round of the OHSAA postseason will be Oct. 30. The top four teams in each region will again receive byes into the quarterfinal round starting Nov. 6.

This season will see the Division I, II, III and V state championship games take place on Friday, Dec. 4 — one of which will move to Thursday. The D-IV, VI and VII championship games will be on Saturday, Dec. 5.

Coaching movesRyan Jones moves over from Versailles to take the role at Troy.

A trio of moves in the SWBL see Matt Root now in charge at Edgewood, Brad Hunt taking over at Monroe, and Joe Fullenkamp at Brookville.

There are two OHC changes with Cooper Chaffin taking over at Greenon, and Tim Melvin getting the coach role at Triad. Geron Stokes is back at Urbana. Versailles AD Scott Broerman will take over for Jones.

Two switches in the WOAC have Chris Goodwin in charge at Bradford, while a late move saw Ricky St. Augustine take over at National Trail.

Kevin Scholz is the new coach at Clinton-Massie, replacing longtime head coach Dan McSurley. Zach Williams was hired to lead Wilmington.

Rule changesThere are a few changes to the rule book for the 2026 season.

The National Federal of State High School Associations approved play cards to be worn on the wrist or belt areas of the uniform.

Any fumble that falls forward and goes out of bounds before it is recovered will be returned to the original spot where the fumble occurred.

Players will not be allowed to use their hands to slap an opponent’s head, while some mouth protector attachments will be restricted.

Officials will be placing an emphasis on defenseless player and targeting fouls. They also will emphasize sportsmanship, and getting players to follow equipment rules.

No league realignmentWhile many recent years have seen schools leave one conference and begin their tenure in another, the 2026-27 school year will be status quo in the Miami Valley.

Starting in the Fall of 2027, however, the Central Buckeye Conference, Ohio Heritage Conference, Southwestern Buckeye League, and Three Rivers Conference all will look different with Bethel, Dayton Christian, Greenon, Riverside and Talawanda set to complete league switches.

New two-year enrollment cycle and competitive balance counts start this season and with it numerous OHSAA division changes.

One of the most notable reassignments sees reigning D-VII state champion St. Henry going up to D-VI.

Troy – which finished the 2025 season as the top seed in Region 2 – moves back down to D-II.

Two GWOC schools are on the move again as Miamisburg goes back up to D-I, while Northmont was expected to go down to D-II, but petitioned to stay in Division I.

A trio of Butler County schools are all moving up to D-II – Badin (due to competitive balance number adjustments), Ross and Talawanda.

Monroe bumps down to D-III. West Carrollton does the same after CB adjustments.

Other moves upward include Region 24 champ Coldwater going up to D-V, as well as Bethel (D-III), Thurgood Marshall (D-III), Northridge (D-IV), Dayton Christian (D-V), and Stivers (D-V).

Going down are Dunbar (D-IV), Brookville (D-V), Northwestern (D-V), Versailles (D-VI), and Triad (D-VII).

Tecumseh (D-III) and Kenton Ridge (D-IV) had enrollment bumps that would have moved both of them up one division before CB adjustments kept them where they were last year. Alter (D-III) and Troy Christian (D-VI) had the reverse occur, staying put instead of going down.

Significant moves across the state include reigning D-III state champion Columbus Bishop Watterson going up to D-II after CB, as is runner-up Toledo Central Catholic. D-V champion Liberty Center also moves down to D-VI.

Firing out of the gateThe Kettering rivalry of Alter vs. Fairmont gets the season started on Thursday, Aug. 20. Week 1 will get underway in full force with the first Friday slate taking place the following evening. St. Xavier at Lakota West, Centerville at Lakota East, and Winton Woods at Springfield are among the exciting games.

Week 2 has several intriguing matchups as Fairmont goes to Trotwood, Wayne hosts St. Xavier, and league play starts in the GMC with Lakota East playing at Lakota West, as well as in the MVL when Troy visits Xenia.

Lakewood St. Edward plays at Wayne in a marquee Week 3 game. The same night sees Middletown visit Fairfield, and Trotwood facing Springfield.

title: Tarik Skubal greets new Dodgers teammates during game versus Red Sox
description: Los Angeles' new pitcher arrived in the dugout during the third inning Sunday.
fullText:

New Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal created a grand entrance.

Acquired from the Detroit Tigers on Saturday night for three prospects, Skubal showed up in the Dodgers' dugout during the third inning of the Dodgers' matchup against the visiting Boston Red Sox on Sunday night.

The back-to-back AL Cy Young award winner was immediately greeted by Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who had time during a pitching change to embrace Skubal. They chatted for about a minute before Roberts had to get back to work.

Skubal proceeded to walk down the dugout, introducing himself to his new teammates.

Skubal (7-5), who is scheduled to make his Dodgers debut Tuesday at the Chicago Cubs, joins a stacked rotation that entered Sunday with the league's best WHIP (1.14) and ranked fourth in ERA (3.60).

The salaries of the Dodgers' top six starters, Skubal, Shohei Ohtani, Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, Edwin Diaz and Yoshinobu Yamamoto would create the league's 18th-highest team payroll.

Four of the Dodgers' starters had sub-3.00 ERAs, Ohtani (1.79), Skubal (2.79), Yamamoto (2.79) and Justin Wrobleski (2.88).

title: Nationals Announce Trade with Yankees, Additional Pitching Moves
description: The Luis García Jr trade with the New York Yankees has officially been announced, while the Washington Nationals announced additional pitching moves.
fullText:
Roughly one hour after news broke, the second pre-deadline trade for the Washington Nationals was officially announced after sending Luis Garcia Jr. to the New York Yankees in exchange for four right handed pitchers: Jake Bird, Yovanny Cruz, Jack Cebert and Ben Grable.

While Cebert and Grable are in the second year of their professional careers after the Yankees selected both in last year's draft and are possibilities on the 2027 roster, Cruz and Bird arrive with MLB experience. Cruz touched 100 mph in his MLB debut, while also posting a 1.69 ERA and holding opponents to a .167 batting average across his first four MLB games. Bird, 30, arrives with plenty more experience having pitched in over 220 games after two seasons with the Yankees was followed by four seasons with the Colorado Rockies.

Bird allowed six earned runs across four games in his first season with the Yankees before then posting a 5.53 ERA and 1.54 WHIP across 36 appearances in 2026. The Nationals announced that Bird will begin his tenure with the organization in Triple A Rochester, but there are additional reinforcements on the way in the future.

Grable, rated the 19th-best prospect in the Yankees' farm system prior to the trade, was named a late replacement in the All Star Futures Game that Eli Willits and Miguel Sime also appeared in. Yet it's been his power that has been hard to ignore with his fastball touching 99 mph in 2026, adding young talent to potentially address the Nationals' biggest current weakness along the roster.

Yet it also came at a cost after the Nationals traded its longest tenured player in Luis García Jr. to the Yankees in exchange for the four right handed pitchers, giving president of baseball operations Paul Toboni the opportunity to sell high on the infielder who has enjoyed a breakout season under first-year manager Blake Butera.

While Andres Chaparro and Brady House will look to become to stopgaps at first base through the rest of the regular season, Garcia's presence will be a tough one to fill. CJ Abrams pointed to Garcia as the one who he first connected with the now star shortstop after first arriving in Washington DC via trade. Yet a potential divorce became growingly apparent through the month with growing noise about outside interest -- and the Nationals' willingness to listen.

Garcia noted the opportunity to head to the Yankees marks a "new chapter" in his career, but the chance to end his time in Washington in a season that has surpassed expectations marked the high note.

"A lot of great memories. A lot of great moments over my tenure here with the Nationals, and all I can say is that I love this organization. I love my teammates, the clubhouse, the coaches, staff, everyone."

While the Nationals are expected to announce additional roster moves ahead of Monday's series against the Philadelphia Phillies, Washington announced following the trade that Riley Cornelio will join Bird in Rochester, while PJ Poulin has also been transferred to the 60 day injured list.

title: Bears Teammates Highlight Garrett Bradbury's Communication Skills in Camp
description: Following Drew Dalman’s retirement, veteran center Garrett Bradbury has impressed teammates with a seamless transition, providing the veteran leadership and vocal presence for the Chicago Bears' offensive line.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears finally had stable play from the center position last season.

Drew Dalman played every offensive snap and earned himself a Pro Bowl nod. After years of instability on the interior spot of the offensive line, there was finally consistency.

Dalman retired in March, and the Bears quickly traded for New England Patriots center Garrett Bradbury. The veteran offensive lineman has seven years of NFL experience and 105 starts to his name.

Although he's the new guy on the Bears' O-line, his teammates haven't noticed a drop off in the operation of head coach Ben Johnson's offense.

"I think we were all a little, you know, you don't know how it's going to go, especially when we lose somebody like Drew, who's, you know, kind of that captain of the offensive line there communication wise," Bears tight end Cole Kmet said. "But, I mean, with Garrett, it really has been flawless so far, and I know we haven't had pads on from a physicality standpoint, but, you know, you talked about communication in the walkthroughs that we've had, and in practice, things have been really clear, concise, and I feel like when I've been out there, especially in the run game and the pass pro, things have been really clear. And I think we've had great understanding with one another, so yeah, it's a good unit up front for sure."

Braxton Jones is currently in a competition for the starting left tackle position, but he's also noticed the cohesion he's felt with Bradbury playing with the starting unit.

"I mean, Garrett's jumped right in," Jones said. "He's, I mean, it's almost, it's weird like, you know, shoutout to Drew Dalman and everything he did, but, you know, Garrett jumped right in and has done a great job. It's like, you know, the same thing, their communication is great. And, you know, obvioulsy Garrett's a hell of a player himself, so it's been great and the continuity going forward. We're all a brotherhood. We all have a good time, but whe it's ready to, you know, get that work in, we're all getting that work in. So, it's just a great group to be around.

Caleb Williams is now playing with his third center in the last three years. The center and quarterback relationship is an important one for any offense. After last Wednesday's training camp practice, he mentioned that there was a slight miscommunication between the two.

Training camp is the time to address those miscues, as the Bears' quarterback is looking for perfection on game days.

Garrett doesn't have to be perfect -- or Dalman -- but he does need to provide a stable presence at the center position for this Bears offense to reach its next level.

title: Blue Jays make trade, send 2-time All-Star to Cubs
description: The Blue Jays cut ties with a pitcher who won 53 games over the previous five seasons
fullText:
Kevin Gausman’s five-year run with the Toronto Blue Jays included one All-Star team, one pennant, and 53 wins, making him one of the most reliable starting pitchers in the American League.

That run ended Sunday, August 2, when the Blue Jays traded Gausman to the Chicago Cubs, according to a new report.

Ken Rosenthal and Mitch Bannon of The Athletic reported Gausman was traded to the Cubs, who are hungry for starting pitchers as they chase down a playoff berth.

MORE: Father of Blue Jays pitcher dies while visiting family on team’s road trip

According to Bannon, the Blue Jays will receive outfielder Brett Bateman and infielder Ty Southisene in return. Southisene, 21, was playing for the Cubs’ advanced Class-A affiliate. Bateman, 24, saw time at all three outfield positions with the Cubs’ Triple-A affiliate.

The MLB trade deadline is less than 24 hours away. Coincidentally, the Blue Jays acquired pitcher Jameson Taillon in a trade with the Cubs on Saturday.

MORE: Blue Jays acquire former Cubs pitcher one day before trade deadline

Gausman, 35, is 5-10 with a 4.38 ERA in 23 starts this season. He’s in the final year of a five-year, $110 million contract. The Cubs were not among the eight teams to which Gausman could block a trade.

The right-hander is among the most durable pitchers in baseball. He hasn’t made fewer than 30 starts in a non-pandemic season this decade. Last year he threw a career-high 193 innings with a 3.59 ERA in the regular season, then made an additional six postseason appearances and posted a 2.93 ERA as the Blue Jays took the Dodgers to Game 7 of the World Series.

MORE: Dodgers, Tigers finalizing Tarik Skubal trade

The Cubs’ starting rotation has been decimated by injuries this season. Gausman might not have the stuff to replace injured ace Justin Steele at this stage of his career, but he could help cover innings as the Cubs look to close the gap in the National League Wild Card race.

At 63-49, the Cubs currently hold the NL’s top Wild Card position.

title: Three quarterbacks battle for Southern University starting role
description: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — Southern first-year head coach Marshall Faulk has told the media multiple times that he wants to name a starting quarterback as early as possible. That’s a welcome change of pace for Jag fans, who have grown accustomed to not knowing who the starter is until the week or day […]
fullText:
BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — Southern first-year head coach Marshall Faulk has told the media multiple times that he wants to name a starting quarterback as early as possible.

That’s a welcome change of pace for Jag fans, who have grown accustomed to not knowing who the starter is until the week or day of the season opener.

SWAC releases 2026 preseason poll; Southern picked fifth in West

Faulk still hasn’t officially named a starting quarterback, but after the first day of fall camp, the competition appears to be narrowing.

Christian Johnson (transfer from Hutchinson Community College), Ashton Strother, and Wyatt McCaulley (transfer from Long Beach City College) were the three quarterbacks taking snaps under center. Johnson received the first-team reps, followed by Strother and McCaulley.

Strother is the only returning quarterback from last season. He appeared in nine games, totaling 1,202 all-purpose yards, eight touchdowns, and five interceptions.

For the other quarterbacks on the roster, Faulk says he still plans on getting them involved, just in different roles.

We should get an official announcement on who the Jags’ starting quarterback will be sometime this week.

title: Eala vs. Pegula Final Halted Again: Resume Time Revealed
description: Alex Eala had begun to find a foothold in the Mubadala DC Open final when severe weather intervened again.The women’s championship match between Eala and Jessica Pegula was suspended Sunday because of rain and lightning near the Rock Creek Park Tennis Center in Washington. Pegula led 6-4, 1-2 when the players left Stadium Court, with […] The post Eala vs. Pegula Final Halted Again: Resume Time Revealed appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Alex Eala had begun to find a foothold in the Mubadala DC Open final when severe weather intervened again.

The women’s championship match between Eala and Jessica Pegula was suspended Sunday because of rain and lightning near the Rock Creek Park Tennis Center in Washington. Pegula led 6-4, 1-2 when the players left Stadium Court, with the match on serve in the second set.

Tournament organizers announced that the final would resume no earlier than 7:00 p.m. Eastern time. That corresponds to 7:00 a.m. Monday in the Philippines.

The women's final will resume NB 7:00pm. We will continue to provide updates.

While waiting for the rain to clear, please enjoy our various restaurant partners across the grounds. If you want to leave & return after the rain clears, fans will be readmitted at both gates.

— Mubadala DC Open (@mubadaladcopen) August 2, 2026

The restart remained contingent upon the rain clearing and the court being dried and deemed safe for play.

Shortly before 6 p.m., the tournament announced that lightning was no longer in the vicinity and spectators on-site were free to move around the grounds. That lifted one immediate safety restriction, but organizers had not moved up the 6:30 p.m. target for the resumption.

“We will continue to provide updates,” the tournament said.

Fans were permitted to leave the venue during the delay and return once conditions improved. Tournament officials said ticketholders would be readmitted through both gates and encouraged those who remained to visit the restaurant partners across the grounds.

Sunday’s final had already endured a lengthy weather delay before Eala and Pegula finally walked onto Stadium Court.

Originally scheduled for noon, the match was pushed back several times as rain moved through Washington. When play eventually began, Pegula made the steadier start and claimed the opening set 6-4.

The world No. 3 converted two of her three break-point opportunities, while Eala went 1-for-4. Pegula also enjoyed considerably more success behind her second serve, winning seven of 13 such points. Eala won only three of nine.

Despite the narrow scoreline, Pegula’s ability to absorb Eala’s left-handed patterns and redirect the ball early gave the American an edge in the most important exchanges.

Eala remained within reach by winning 13 of 18 points behind her first serve. Her second delivery, however, was vulnerable against one of the best returners on the WTA Tour.

Pegula served out the set to move within one set of her third title this season and the 12th singles championship of her career.

Eala emerged with renewed purpose in the second set.

The 21-year-old Filipina held her first two service games and moved ahead 2-1 without facing a break point. She won all seven points played behind her first serve in the set and nine of 13 service points overall.

That improvement offered Eala a path back into the match before rain and nearby lightning interrupted her momentum. The players left Stadium Court after 55 minutes of play, with neither woman having faced a break point in the second set.

Eala is attempting to capture her first tour-level singles championship in her second WTA final. Her run through Washington has included victories over Zheng Qinwen, defending champion Leylah Fernandez, world No. 10 Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

Pegula is seeking her second Washington title, seven years after winning her maiden WTA trophy at the same tournament.

The American defeated Eala in their only previous meeting, surviving a three-set battle in the 2025 Miami Open semifinals. Their long-awaited rematch has become another struggle — against each other and the uncooperative Washington sky.

title: Blue Jays reportedly trade Kevin Gausman to Cubs, signaling sell-off months after World Series appearance
description: The deal in part signals a Blue Jays selloff at the MLB trade deadline, months after they took the Dodgers to extra innings in Game 7 of the World Series.
fullText:
The Toronto Blue Jays have traded starting pitcher Kevin Gausman to the Chicago Cubs, signaling a sell-off at the MLB trade deadline months after they took the Dodgers to extra innings in Game 7 of the World Series.

The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Mitch Bannon reported the trade on Sunday, hours before Monday's 6 p.m. ET trade deadline. In return, according to the report, the Blue Jays will receive outfielder Brett Bateman and infielder Ty Southisene, both prospects.

The move in part cements a season of disappointment for the Blue Jays, who started 2026 with hopes of competing for the AL East title and returning to the postseason. Instead, they've entered the stretch run in last place in the division at 52-60 with long-shot hopes of competing for a wild-card spot.

Whether the Blue Jays would be sellers at the deadline or hold steady for a shot at the postseason was unclear before the All-Star break. But they lost five of their first six games coming out of the break, including three to the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays.

Gausman is playing on the final season of a five-year, $110 million contract. He was a prime candidate for a deadline deal to a contending team seeking a contributor with an expiring contract.

A two-time All-Star, Gausman isn't at his peak form at 35 years old. But he's been a reliable starter for much of his career, including this season as one of MLB's leaders in starts and innings pitched.

Gausman provides the Cubs with a mid-rotation option days after they designated veteran Jameson Taillon for assignment.

Taillon, 34, was in the midst of a career-worst season with a 5.92 ERA and 25 home runs allowed. Chicago traded Taillon to Toronto in a separate deal earlier Sunday for cash considerations or a player to be named later.

Taillon pitched 76 innings for the Cubs this season, and his departure left Chicago with a hole in their rotation. Gausman, who's made 14 postseason appearances, slots in for what the Cubs hope is an upgrade for the stretch run and a likely playoff appearance.

The Cubs leave a 2-1 loss to the Yankees on Sunday at 63-49, in control of first place in the NL wild-card standings with a four-game cushion over second. They're 6.5 game behind the Brewers for first place in the NL Central.

Per MLB Pipeline, Southisene ranked as Chicago's No. 13 prospect, and Bateman rated at No. 21. Neither are in MLB Pipeline's top 100 overall prospects. They're both now building blocks for Toronto's future.

title: Here’s When Tarik Skubal Will Make His Los Angeles Dodgers Debut
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers made headlines late Saturday night when they acquired back-to-back Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers.In exchange, Los Angeles sent MLB’s No. 25 prospect, outfielder Zyhir Hope, along with right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith to Detroit.The Dodgers made the trade official Sunday and quickly revealed when Skubal […] The post Here’s When Tarik Skubal Will Make His Los Angeles Dodgers Debut appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made headlines late Saturday night when they acquired back-to-back Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers.

In exchange, Los Angeles sent MLB’s No. 25 prospect, outfielder Zyhir Hope, along with right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith to Detroit.

The Dodgers made the trade official Sunday and quickly revealed when Skubal will make his team debut.

Skubal made his final start for the Tigers on Wednesday against the Baltimore Orioles, and the Dodgers are keeping him on his regular schedule.

As a result, Skubal will make his Dodgers debut Tuesday night when the team faces the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field.

Tarik Skubal will officially make his Dodgers debut on Tuesday at Wrigley Field, per @ByJackHarris pic.twitter.com/GnCVNSZ84u

— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) August 2, 2026

Skubal reacted to the trade early Sunday morning in an interview, saying he was “excited to be a Dodger.”

“I’m excited to be a Dodger,” Skubal said to reporters, via Detroit SportsNet. “I’m excited to get down there and meet all those guys, and chase three championships in a row. That’s hard to do. So I’m excited to be a part of that. But yeah, it’s a lot of different emotions. Definitely kind of a roller coaster a little bit.”

The Dodgers are coming off two straight losses against the Boston Red Sox entering Sunday’s series finale.

Los Angeles currently sits at 69-42 and is tied with the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in MLB.

For the time being, Skubal will join a rotation featuring Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan, Roki Sasaki, and Eric Lauer.

However, when fully healthy, the Dodgers will likely be adding Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow to the mix.

title: Postseason baseball: Watertown Post 17 makes run, state amateur pairings set
description: Watertown Post 17 went 2-2 and tied for third in the South Dakota State Class A American Legion Baseball Tournament at Rapid City.
fullText:
RAPID CITY — Another strong postseason run by the Watertown Arrows Post 17 baseball team ended with an 8-0 loss to Sioux Falls West in the 2026 state Class A American Legion Baseball Tournament.

Post 17, which went a combined 38-25 over the high school and Legion seasons in 2026, went 2-2 in the tourney and finished as one of the final four teams in the tourney.

Watertown opened the tourney on Tuesday, July 28 with a 10-2 loss to eventual champion Rapid City Post 22. Post 17 then beat Brandon Valley 5-3 in eight innings on July 29 and Rapid City Post 320 7-0 on July 30 before coming up short against Sioux Falls West.

"As the No. 10 seed, we knew we were going to have to play outstanding baseball if we wanted to stay in the tournament, and I thought our guys did exactly that over the course of four days," Post 17 coach Ryan Neale said. "Our only two losses came against the two teams that played for the state championship."

Here are some highlights from each of Post 17's state tourney games:

Rapid City Post 22 10, Watertown 2 — Post 22 plated four runs in the bottom of the first inning and rolled to the win. Cole Hansen and Sam Olson each had two hits for Post 17.

Watertown 5, Brandon Valley 3 — Brandon Valley grabbed a 3-0 lead in the first. Watertown cut the lead to 3-2 on Carter Buisker's two-run single in the fifth, tied the game on Cain Everson's safety squeeze bunt in the seventh and won the game on Jaxon Falak's two-out, two-run single in the top of the eighth. Hunter Halajain struck out six batters in seven strong innings, and Buisker recorded the final two outs for the save.

Watertown 7, Rapid City Post 320 0 — Jackson McClemans, who started and took the loss against RC Post 22 in the tourney opener, tossed the complete-game shutout in this game. He allowed six hits and fanned four batters for Post 17, which plated five runs in the bottom of the first on a three-run homer by Markus Pitkin and a two-run single by Ashton Rabine. Pitkin also doubled and finished with four RBIs.

Sioux Falls West 8, Watertown 0 — West scored two runs apiece in the bottom of the first, second, fourth and fifth innings. Everson had two of Watertown's six hits, and Olson added a double."

"I couldn't be more proud of what this team accomplished," Neale added. "To finish tied for third after entering as the No. 10 seed says a lot about the character of this group."

Host Rapid City Post 22 (49-12) completed a 5-0 run in the tourney by beating Yankton 4-3 on July 31 and Sioux Falls West 8-3 in the championship on Aug. 1. The state title was the 45th for Post 22, which advances to the Central Plains Regional Aug. 5-9 at Mandan, ND.

Post 22 second baseman and Nebraska recruit Wyatt Reeder, who batted .769 (10-for-13), received the Big Stick and MVP awards in the tourney. Sioux Falls West received the Porter T. Talcott Sportsmanship Award.

In other postseason baseball highlights this week:

MADISON — Host Madison clinched a berth in the tourney championship by beating Volga 4-3 on Quincy Kurtz's walk-off single with two outs in the bottom of the seventh inning on Sunday, Aug. 2.

Braden Danzeisen homered and singled for Volga.

Sunday, Aug. 2 — In elimination games, Dakota Valley beat Groton 8-4, and Dell Rapids turned back Parkston 9-7. Sterling Schauff had three hits for Dakota Valley and Jordan Schwan homered and doubled for Groton. Gauge Bunkers and Haiden Kaffar each drove in three runs for Dell Rapids.

Saturday, Aug. 1 — Dell Rapids downed Garretson 211-9 and Dakota Valley topped Belle Fource 12-10 in elimination games. Connor Hanson drove in three runs for Dell Rapids. Jack Jones had three hits for Dakota Valley. In the winner's bracket, Volga scored three runs in the top of the first and held off Groton 4-3, and Madison beat Parkston 9-2. Wyatt Hardt hit a bases-clearing triple and Tate Steffensen added two hits to back Damon Uecker's solid pitching for Volga. TC Schuster had three hits for Groton. Casyn Crabtree fired a three-hitter with seven strikeouts and JD Prorok homered for Madison.

Friday, July 31 — Volga beat Dell Rapids 3-1 behind Hardt, who tossed a four-hitter with a double and single, and Trentyn Schmit, who hit a two-run single. Parkston topped Belle Fourche 7-2 with two hits by Kolter Kramer and two RBIs from Jaxx Kurtenach. Groton held off Garretson 3-2 with Jarrett Erdmann (5 2/3, 3 hits) and Nick Groeblinghoff (1 1/3, 1 hit) teaming on a four-hitter and Schwan and Karsten Fliehs each delivering run-scoring hits. Cale Johnson's two-run homer in the top of the 10th inning helped host Madison close the day with a 6-4 win over Dakota Valley.

SIOUX FALLS — Watertown Post 17 went 0-3 in the state tournament that was held Thursday, July 30 through Sunday, Aug. 2 at Harmodon Park.

Post 17 (33-24) opened pool play with a 13-3 loss to the Renner Post 307 Kings on July 30. Kaeden Himmerich and Caleb Kannas each had two hits for Watertown.

Harrisburg Gold topped Watertown 5-3 on July 31. Levi Lund drove in two runs for Post 17, which got singles from Taren Veflin and Kannas.

Watertown closed out the tournament with a 12-3 pool-play loss to Sioux Falls East on Aug. 1. Kannas had two hits in the loss.

Brandon Valley Black downed Harrisburg Gold 11-1 in the semifinals and Renner 9-5 in the championship on Aug. 2. Renner advanced to the finals with a 5-4 win over the Rapid City Post 320 Shooters.

MORE BASEBALL: Postseason tournaments held for Legion, Junior Legion, amateur & other levels

Redfield went 3-1 and outlasted Volga to win the Region 6B tournament July 27-29 at Clark. Volga, which went 3-2, came out of the consolation bracket to beat Redfield 16-15 in 8 innings on July 29 before Redfield followed with a 14-4 win. Tate Bray went 3-for-5 with a double, triple and three RBIs in the final game.

Both teams will play in the state tourney Aug. 7-9 at Redfield.

Sisseton also qualified for the tourney by going 3-1 and winning the Region 1B tourney July 27-29 in Sisseton. Groton came out of the consolation bracket to beat Sisseton 12-8 on July 29 (getting two hits and four RBIs from T.C. Schuster and three hits each from Zach and Braden Fliehs) before Sisseton won the final game 7-4 with two RBIs each from JJ Hamm and Karter Deutsch.

The state tourney opens on Aug. 7 with Winner-Colome facing Volga at 10 a.m., followed by Madison vs. Canton (30 minutes after Game 1) and Dakota Valley vs. Parkston (30 minutes after Game 2). title: Dennis Buzukja Reacts Following After UFC Belgrade Stoppage
description: UFC featherweight fighter Dennis Buzukja reacted following the controversial stoppage loss he suffered to Bogdan Grad at UFC Belgrade.With seconds left to go in the second round, referee Jason Herzog stopped the fight, as he believed that Buzukja tapped to a Grad arm-triangle choke. However, Buzukja immediately protested the stoppage, and on replay, it was […] The post Dennis Buzukja Reacts Following After UFC Belgrade Stoppage appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
UFC featherweight fighter Dennis Buzukja reacted following the controversial stoppage loss he suffered to Bogdan Grad at UFC Belgrade.

With seconds left to go in the second round, referee Jason Herzog stopped the fight, as he believed that Buzukja tapped to a Grad arm-triangle choke. However, Buzukja immediately protested the stoppage, and on replay, it was not clear that he tapped out, leading to frustration from fans on social media, many of whom felt that Herzog stopped the fight too early.

Following the loss, Buzukja took to his social media to react to the loss, with the featherweight clearly being frustrated with Herzog stopping the fight when he didn’t clearly tap out.

“I don’t know what to say. It was a war and went in there to win or die. To have the fight stopped and stolen from me like that with no tap or submission I don’t understand. But no matter what it’s God’s will always. Respect to my opponent Bogdan. I don’t understand how the referee stopped it or why he thought I tapped out when the choke wasn’t tight and 10 seconds left. I don’t know what to do from here or where I’ll go from here but I just want to say thank you to everyone. I’m very heartbroken and feel like it would’ve been an amazing third round but this is life,” Buzukja wrote on his Instagram.

Following the loss to Grad at UFC Belgrade, Buzukja’s UFC record dropped to 1-5, so he is at serious risk of losing his roster spot as a result of this defeat, which makes things even more frustrating for him.

Buzukja was originally signed to the UFC following a win on Dana White’s Contender Series in 2022. Since then, he has won just one fight in the Octagon, a knockout victory over Connor Matthews in 2024.

Buzukja better hope that the UFC matchmakers agree with him that this was a bad stoppage and that he gets one more chance to prove himself. But if he does get released, it wouldn’t be a surprise.

title: Kamilla Rakhimova beats Venus Williams 6-4, 6-1 in a rain-delayed match in Toronto
description: Kamilla Rakhimova beat Venus Williams 6-4, 6-1 in a rain-delayed match Sunday to kick off the National Bank Open women’s main draw.  Granted a singles wild-card entry at the WTA 1000 event, the 46-year-old Williams has lost 12 straight matches dating to July 2025.  “We play outside … you can’t control the weather,” Williams said.
fullText:
TORONTO (AP) — Kamilla Rakhimova beat Venus Williams 6-4, 6-1 in a rain-delayed match Sunday to kick off the National Bank Open women’s main draw.

Granted a singles wild-card entry at the WTA 1000 event, the 46-year-old Williams has lost 12 straight matches dating to July 2025.

“We play outside … you can’t control the weather,” Williams said. “But the fans were amazing. They were with me right in every point — that was fantastic. I was just fighting to put the ball on the court."

The 24-year-old Rakhimova is from Uzbekistan. She's ranked 82nd in the world.

“Playing Venus is not an everyday experience,” Rakhimova said. “I’m very glad to actually get a chance to play against her. I was looking forward to that match. I knew it was going to be a center-court match. I was trying to enjoy my time on it, no matter what the result."

title: Former Maple Leafs Forward Sends Blunt Message To Brandon Duhaime
description: It’s been a summer of change for the Toronto Maple Leafs, who have made significant shifts in leadership both behind the bench as well as their front office. As part of his multiple moves since taking over from the fired Brad Treliving, general manager John Chayka has brought aboard several new faces while also bidding […] The post Former Maple Leafs Forward Sends Blunt Message To Brandon Duhaime appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It’s been a summer of change for the Toronto Maple Leafs, who have made significant shifts in leadership both behind the bench as well as their front office. As part of his multiple moves since taking over from the fired Brad Treliving, general manager John Chayka has brought aboard several new faces while also bidding goodbye to several others.

One of the new faces in Toronto for the upcoming season is forward Brandon Duhaime, who agreed to a three-year, $7.8 million deal to join the Maple Leafs after having played the last two seasons as a member of the Washington Capitals.

And according to a notable former member of the Maple Leafs, there’s a specific way that Duhaime can endear himself to his new fanbase in the upcoming campaign.

While making an appearance on Leafs Morning Take, former Maple Leafs forward Jay Rosehill, who is now an analyst, said that the addition of Duhaime can pay off for the Maple Leafs as they look to get back to the Stanley Cup Playoffs.

“Duhaime for me,” Rosehill said. “I think that he can play gritty. I think he can play with a chip on his shoulder.”

“You talk about a guy dumping it and going and doing something,” Rosehill continued. “I think that he can bring that energy.”

Additionally, Rosehill believes that the kind of energy that Duhaime plays with can help bring life to Scotiabank Arena, which has garnered a reputation for having too much of a corporate atmosphere.

“We talk about the building all the time being quiet,” he said. “We talk about the bottom six doing sweet FA with the minutes that they’re giving.”

With that style of play, Duhaime can quickly become a fan favorite in Toronto.

“I think Duhaime’s a guy who can go out there and get it,” Rosehill said. “To be honest, it’s playing a little bit nasty. It’s playing physical. It’s playing hard. It’s playing rugged. It’s causing some shit out there. I’m looking forward to watching that.”

“I think he has a chance to get in there, be physical, and win some hearts of some fans over this season.”

Duhaime was taken 106th overall by the Minnesota Wild in the 2016 NHL Draft while playing for Providence College, and he would eventually make his debut with the club in 2021-22, appearing in 80 games and scoring six goals with 11 assists.

He also played two seasons with their American Hockey League affiliate Iowa Wild.

Duhaime would be traded by the Wild to the divisional rival Colorado Avalanche in 2024, and he would have to face Minnesota in his first game with his new Avalanche teammates. Following the season, he’d agree to a two-year contract with the Washington Capitals.

So far in his NHL career, Duhaime has appeared in 375 games, and has scored 33 goals with 37 assists. He’s also added four goals and one assist in 33 Stanley Cup Playoff games.
