title: ‘Coward’: Caitlin Clark sparks outrage for not backing Sophie Cunningham’s trans comments
description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has found her niche off the bench this season, has become a household name. Interestingly, Cunningham’s rapid rise is more about her views off the court than it is about her play on it. In a July 21 ESPN profile, Cunningham commented on what she felt was necessary to…
fullText:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has found her niche off the bench this season, has become a household name. Interestingly, Cunningham’s rapid rise is more about her views off the court than it is about her play on it.

In a July 21 ESPN profile, Cunningham commented on what she felt was necessary to “protect women’s sports.”

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” she told the Worldwide Leader after being asked about the “MAGA Barbie” nickname some fans have given her.

“I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

Local media approached Cunningham about the comments a few days later and she doubled down.

“I said what I said. I think it’s kind of common sense,” she said. “And I think I’ll always believe in that. I think it’s really important to protect children, and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said.”

Cunningham’s stance has turned into a frenzied debate, with people from all corners of sports media, the White House, and multiple head coaches across the WNBA weighing in. Fever star Caitlin Clark has avoided the media since the controversy began, until her post-game session following Sunday’s defeat to the Minnesota Lynx, when she was curt in addressing the situation.

“It’s for the leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. My focus is on basketball” Clark said.

Caitlin Clark refused to back Sophie Cunningham:

“It’s for the leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. My focus is on basketball.” pic.twitter.com/R7HfzZIKwC

— BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) August 3, 2026

Some of Cunningham’s staunchest supporters on social media were furious that Clark didn’t say anything in support of her teammate.

“Sophie backs you all day everyday … and you can’t hold that same respect with common sense? Hmmmmm. Don’t like this look,” one fan posted on X.

“Coward. Everyone’s so scared to fight back… I refuse to participate in their fairytales. There’s males and females. Point blank,” someone else added.

“Caitlin Clark bailed on the truth a long time ago. She’s not the hero we thought she was,” another fan added.

Considering the Fever lost 108-100 to Minnesota on Sunday, it’s probably for the best that Clark is keeping the focus on basketball, and with Cunningham only scoring three points in the contest, she may want to refocus on what’s happening on teh court as well.

title: IMSA 2026 Road America results: Wayne Taylor Racing snaps long winless streak in GTP
description: The team wins a chaotic six-hour race for its first victory since June 2024.
fullText:
Wayne Taylor Racing ended a winning streak of more than two years in IMSA Grand Touring Prototype, winnin the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix at Road America with the No. 10 Cadillac of Filipe Albuquerque and Ricky Taylor

In a chaotic race (expanded to six hours) Sunday on the Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin, road course, Albuquerque and Taylor delivered the team's first win in the top category of the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship since Detroit in June 2024. It's WTR's first victory since returning to Cadillac last year.

"Very, very special," Albuquerque said. "This is more than just a win. Super happy with everyone.”

Albuquerque took the lead from Jack Aitken in the No. 31 Cadillac with just under 90 minutes remaining and held on through multiple restarts as the race ended under yellow. The No. 5 JDC-Miller MotorSports Porsche 963 of Laurin Heinrich, Kaylen Frederick and Tijmen van der Helm finished second, and WTR 's No. 40 Cadillac of Jordan Taylor and Louis Deletraz finished third.

“Amazing day, it was a full team effort," Ricky Taylor said. "So proud of how the team has stuck with it and kept working towards this sort of result, and just very thankful to Cadillac for sticking with us through all of it. They've always had our back, and they've emphasized how it's one team and that support goes a long way to keeping our confidence because our confidence has been challenged a lot with the lack of results. So, finally getting a win and not just a lucky one. It was a strong performance all day, so we feel like this is something we can build on.”

It's the second win at Road America for Wayne Taylor's team.

“I just couldn't be happier,” Taylor said.“The last 18 months has been the hardest 18 months for me in motorsports that I can remember. I kept saying to myself, we all work hard, we've got great partners, and the drivers are all working hard. The most important thing was keeping everybody positive and keeping the passion. To get a win and a third just shows to me that our work ethic, dedication, and focus as a team has paid off. This is really great and I’m very happy for everyone."

The race featured nine cautions and a few dozen penalties, many for rough driving. More than three hours after the race, official results were pending because IMSA was reviewing an incident between the No. 31 Cadillace and No. 6 Porsche.

LMP2: The Inter Europol Competition team won its second consecutive race with the trio of Jeremy Clarke, Bijoy Garg and Tom Dillmann in the No. 43 ORECA LMP2 07.

GTD Pro: Andrea Caldarelli and Sandy Mitchell won in the Pfaff Motorsports-entered No. 9 Lamborghini Temerario GT3.

GTD: Winward Racing captured its second consecutive victory with Russell Ward, Philip Ellis and Indy Dontje in the No. 57 Mercedes-AMG GT3.

title: Braves acquire Tyler Mahle from San Francisco Giants
description: The Atlanta Braves have struck again in the trade market and this time, they are bringing a starting pitcher to town. According to MLB Insider Robert Murray of FanSided, the Braves are picking up RHP Tyler Mahle from the Giants in exchange for RHP Anthony Molina. More to come, so stay tuned.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves have struck again in the trade market and this time, they are bringing a starting pitcher to town. According to MLB Insider Robert Murray of FanSided, the Braves are picking up RHP Tyler Mahle from the Giants in exchange for RHP Anthony Molina.

The Atlanta Braves are acquiring right-hander Tyler Mahle in a trade with the San Francisco Giants, according to sources familiar with the deal. Anthony Molina is going to the Giants.

— Robert Murray (@ByRobertMurray) August 3, 2026

So far this season, Mahle has put up a 5.13 ERA (125 ERA-) with a 4.38 FIP (108 FIP-) over 18 starts and 94.2 innings pitched so far with the Giants. He signed there as a free agent for one year and $10 million after spending a couple of seasons with Texas and he earned that contract after making 16 starts for the Rangers in 2025 (86.2 innings pitched) and producing a 2.18 ERA (54 ERA-) with a 3.37 FIP (80 FIP-).

Clearly, the Braves think that they’ll be able to get the version of Mahle who was able to do a very solid job of preventing Hard-Hit contact (in 2025, he was 77th percentile of all starting pitchers with 37.1 percent of his batted balls being of the Hard-Hit variety), so this figures to be a job for pitching coach Jeremy Hefner to bring out the best in Mahle while he dons the Braves uniform.

Considering that Anthony Molina hasn’t done much at the big league level for anybody so far (and he’s only thrown five innings for the Braves here in 2026), this is definitely a buy-low type situation for Atlanta. Either way, he’s a starting pitcher who’s been able to at least reach the fifth inning in 16 of his 18 starts — though he did have a wobble in his last outing on this past Saturday, which is when he gave up five runs in 5.2 innings against the Padres. He did strike out nine batters (and has a strikeout percentage of 22 percent with a walk rate of 9.2 percent), so there’s that.

Either way, he may not be a front-end type starter for the Braves but he certainly figures to be an okay one if Hefner can do a job and help Mahle cook on the mound while he’s here. I’d imagine that there will be more to come from Atlanta going forward, so we’ll see what happens next.

title: Bam Adebayo reacts to LeBron James choosing the Philadelphia 76ers over the Miami Heat
description: Bam Adebayo and the Heat tried to recruit LeBron James, but it did not work out.
fullText:
Bam Adebayo reacts to LeBron James choosing the Philadelphia 76ers over the Miami Heat originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

After LeBron James announced that he was leaving the Los Angeles Lakers, it led to teams showing interest around the league. Even if he is already 41, LeBron is still one of the most appealing players in the league due to his winning pedigree and tremendous talent.

When he saw the Philadelphia 76ers trade for Jaylen Brown, he saw a team that showed ambition. He was enamored by that, which led to him eventually signing with the 76ers. It was a tough pill to swallow for some teams that wanted to sign him, including his former team, the Miami Heat.

As one of the Heat's stars, Adebayo would have loved to have James setting up for lobs and pick-and-rolls. It would have been an electric trio between Bam, LeBron, and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Unfortunately, it did not pan out for the team from South Beach.

While they managed to sign LeBron 16 years ago, Philly was too enticing to pass up. Adebayo was disappointed because the Heat would have been a much better team, but he is happy with what they have now. Adebayo and Antetokounmpo in the same frontcourt is dangerous, and they know that too.

MORE: Rich Paul believed LeBron James was headed back to Miami

Since Adebayo got close with James during their Team USA days, he is quite familiar with how the four-time Finals MVP thinks. That is why he is not surprised by his decision to join the 76ers, but now, they have to be inter-conference rivals.

"I’m cool with Bron. I consider Bron like a brother, honestly. We’ve been Olympic teammates, but even before that we’ve always had down-to-earth conversations. I’m happy for him. You want what’s best for somebody. That’s really how you go from there," Adebayo said about James joining the 76ers and snubbing the Heat.

The Eastern Conference is quite competitive in the 2026-27 season. Since the New York Knicks are the defending champions, they remain the favorites, but they will have some stiff competition from the Heat, the 76ers, and the resurgent Indiana Pacers with Tyrese Haliburton.

title: Pegula leads Eala as storms push Washington Open finals to Monday
description: World number three Jessica Pegula and rising star Alexandra Eala must wait until Monday to decide a Washington Open champion after thunderstorms postponed the completion of Sunday's WTA final.Eala ousted former world number one Naomi Osaka, second seed Elina Svitolina and defending champion Leylah Fernandez to reach the final.
fullText:
World number three Jessica Pegula and rising star Alexandra Eala must wait until Monday to decide a Washington Open champion after thunderstorms postponed the completion of Sunday's WTA final.

After waiting through a three-hour thunderstorm delay to start, Pegula won the first set 6-4 and Eala led 2-1 in the second set of the championship match when rain returned.

More than five hours passed with conditions remaining unplayable before organizers called off the resumption of play until Monday.

Also postponed was the entire men's final at the WTA and ATP 500-level hardcourt tournament, with 10th-ranked American Taylor Fritz set to face 19-year-old Spaniard Rafael Jodar.

The women's final will resume Monday at noon local time (1600 GMT) with the men's final not before 1 p.m. in Washington.

Pegula, who won her first WTA title in 2019 at Washington, seeks her 12th tour trophy and third of the year after Dubai and Charleston.

The 32-year-old American top seed defeated Eala in a 2025 Miami semi-final in their only prior meeting.

Philippines star Eala, cheered all week by a host of supporters, seeks her first WTA title in her second career final, having lost last year at Eastbourne.

The 21-year-old left-hander is set to jump to a career-best 24th in the world rankings.

Eala ousted former world number one Naomi Osaka, second seed Elina Svitolina and defending champion Leylah Fernandez to reach the final.

Pegula broke Eala in the fifth game, blasting a forehand service return winner, only for Eala to break back at love to 3-3 on a blistering backhand service return winner.

Pegula saved two break points in holding to 4-4, broke again when Eala sent a forehand long in the ninth game and held at love to capture the first set in 40 minutes when Eala hit a backhand beyond the baseline.

Players were on serve and in a changeover when the rain returned.

In 53 minutes before the stoppage, Pegula hit 14 winners to only four by Eala while both had 20 unforced errors.

In the men's final, Fritz seeks an 11th career ATP title and his first since last year at Eastbourne.

Jodar, assured of reaching a career-high 15th in next week's rankings, seeks his second ATP crown after winning at Morocco in April.

title: Braves reportedly acquire SP Tyler Mahle from Giants, further boosting pitching depth
description: Mahle joins Bailey Falter as veteran starting pitchers Atlanta has acquired before Monday's trade deadline.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves are reportedly acquiring starting pitcher Tyler Mahle from the San Francisco Giants for RHP Anthony Molina, per Robert Murray.

Mahle, 31, has started 18 games for the Giants this season. He heads to Atlanta with a 3-9 record and a 5.13 ERA. The Braves won’t be counting on him to become their No. 2 starter, but the veteran arm should be able to eat innings down the stretch of the season to give the franchise an extra option and his teammates some extra rest.

Molina is a 24-year-old pitcher who has made only three appearances for the Braves this season. He saw a lot of work with the Colorado Rockies in his debut season in 2024. That year, he made 35 appearances but finished with a 1-1 record and a 6.79 ERA.

This is the second trade in as many nights that Atlanta has made for starting pitching depth. On Saturday night, the Braves picked up SP Bailey Falter and outfielder Lane Thomas from the Kansas City Royals.

Atlanta was in the market for starting pitching ahead of the trade deadline due to the numerous injuries to the pitching staff. Most recently, Reynaldo Lopez was added to the 15-day IL with left knee inflammation. Spencer Schwellenbach, Hurston Waldrep and Spencer Strider are all also on the IL.

The Braves were tied to Tarik Skubal, but the former Detroit Tigers ace was dealt to the Los Angeles Dodgers on Saturday night. Atlanta was also linked to Tigers SP Casey Mize and could still make a push to acquire him ahead of Monday’s deadline.

title: Luis García Jr. says he is ‘both sad and happy’ for trade to Yankees
description: The Yankees acquired the infielder, who joined the Nationals organization in 2016, on Sunday and sent four pitchers to Washington.
fullText:
ATLANTA — Luis García Jr. wanted to help but could only watch as the Washington Nationals suffered their fifth straight loss on Sunday.

García was scratched about 30 minutes before a 4-2 loss to the Atlanta Braves. He watched the game from the dugout.

A short time later, the New York Yankees announced they got García in a trade with the Nationals in exchange for four pitchers.

“I mean, it was weird, uncomfortable, going out to a dugout and then having all the other teammates look at you,” García said through a translator.

García has spent his career with the Nationals but acknowledged he was excited to move to the Yankees.

“I mean it’s a mix of both sad and happy,” García said. “There’s a new chapter in my career, so yeah, 50-50 right now.”

In exchange for García, the Nationals received right-handed pitchers Jake Bird, Yovanny Cruz, Jack Cebert and Ben Grable.

When asked after Sunday’s 2-1 win at the Chicago Cubs about a trade for García, Yankees manager Aaron Boone was not in a mood to confirm.

The Yankees open a three-game series against the Cardinal in St. Louis on Monday night. There was no official word on whether García would be with the team.

Bird, 30, has a 5.93 ERA in 30 games with the Yankees this season, all in relief. Cruz, 26, has a 1.69 ERA in four games. Grable and Cebert have spent the full season in the minors.

title: Man admits transporting Scottish woman's body in suitcase, Greek police say
description: The man was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, as well as robbery and weapons offences.
fullText:
Greek police say a man has admitted transporting the body of a Scottish woman in a suitcase to an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

Police said Ross, known to her family as Lisa, arrived in Greece on 26 June and stayed in the Piraeus area until 10 July, when she left for an unknown destination in Attica.

After carrying out investigations and analysing video footage, police said they identified a 26-year-old man was connected to the case.

They claim he transported Lisa's body to the abandoned site in a suitcase and subsequently used her bank cards to withdraw money.

During searches carried out at his home, police said a replica pistol and a knife were found and seized.

Lisa had initially stayed in the area of Keratsini, 5.9 miles (9.5km) west of central Athens, with Greek friends.

She had told them that on 15 July she would go to Kypseli, where her "American friends" or acquaintances were.

On Saturday Greek police said they were fast-tracking toxicology reports in order to ascertain the cause of her death, potentially "in the coming days".

Test results can take anywhere from several weeks to a few months depending on the complexity of the case and the workload of forensic laboratories.

They were also looking to trace Lisa's American friends, who they said were also staying in Kypseli.

First Minister John Swinney called it an "absolutely appalling case".

A Scottish government spokesperson said: "This is an extremely distressing time for the family of Elisabeth-Jane Ross and it is important that their privacy is respected while enquiries continue.

"Scottish government officials are in communication with the family and with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to ensure they receive appropriate support.

"As this remains an operational matter for Police Scotland, it would not be appropriate to comment further."

This article originally stated that Greek police had said the suspect had admitted killing Elisabeth-Jane Ross. This was changed after further information emerged.

title: Suicide bomber strikes antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 14
description: A suicide bomber targeted protesters at an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan on Sunday, killing at least 14 people, mostly civilians and police officers, and wounding more than two dozen oth...
fullText:
A suicide bomber targeted protesters at an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan on Sunday, killing at least 14 people, mostly civilians and police officers, and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said.

The attack happened in Kabal, a town in Swat Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where demonstrators had gathered near a police station, chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace, district police chief Omar Khan said.

According to witnesses, shortly before the attack, speakers at the rally said that ensuring security and eliminating militancy were the state's responsibility. They also accused authorities of failing to act decisively against militants, saying residents wanted to live without fear after years of violence that devastated the region.

Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial emergency service, said the attacker struck dozens of people who were chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace. Police official Omar Khan said at least nine civilians and five officers were among the dead.

Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the bombing, expressing deep sorrow over the loss of life. In separate statements, they offered condolences to the families of those killed, prayed for the recovery of the wounded and directed authorities to ensure the wounded receive the best possible medical treatment. Zardari and Sharif also said Pakistan's fight against terrorism would continue until it is eradicated.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also condemned the attack. In a statement, he extending condolences to the families of those killed and prayers for the speedy recovery of the wounded.

The Swat Valley was once a stronghold of Islamic militants who imposed a strict interpretation of Sharia, or Islamic law, before the Pakistani military launched a major operation in 2007 that drove them out and restored government control.

However, militants have resurfaced in the valley in recent months, fueling fears that the Pakistani Taliban are seeking to regain a foothold in the region. In response, residents have repeatedly staged anti-Taliban rallies to protest the militants' presence across the valley.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the bombing, but suspicion is likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, Afghanistan's Taliban rulers. Many of its leaders and fighters have found sanctuary in Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power there in 2021.

Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan's Taliban government of harboring TTP militants, an allegation Kabul denies.

Pakistan has experienced a surge in militant attacks in recent years, particularly targeting police and security forces.

On Friday, Pakistan's military spokesman Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan has recorded 3,145 "terrorism incidents" since January. He said Pakistan had killed 2,084 militants since January, while 819 Pakistanis, including soldiers, police officers and civilians, had been killed.

Chaudhry also said Afghanistan-based militants had carried out 28 suicide attacks in Pakistan since January and alleged that most were carried out by Afghan nationals or people associated with Afghanistan's security forces. He said the TTP and other militant groups were carrying out attacks inside Pakistan with the support of Afghanistan's Taliban rulers and Pakistan would continue to target the TTP and its support infrastructure.

title: Bernie Sanders blasts Fetterman as 'way out of touch' with Americans after Graham Platner rebuke
description: Sen. Bernie Sanders fired back at Sen. John Fetterman on "Meet the Press," citing a Quinnipiac poll showing just 19% approval for Fetterman among Pennsylvania Democrats.
fullText:
Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., criticized Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as "way out of touch" with Americans on Sunday after Fetterman recently accused him of showing no regret over endorsing scandal-plagued former Maine Senate nominee Graham Platner.

Sanders responded by citing Fetterman's standing among Pennsylvania Democrats, arguing that the senator was disconnected from voters on Israel and other issues.

"Well, my response to Fetterman is last time I saw it, he was reflecting the views of about 19% of the Democrats in the state of Pennsylvania," Sanders said on "Meet the Press."

"I think probably lower than any other member of the Democratic Senate. Fetterman does his thing, and I think, on Israel, and many other issues, is way out of touch with the people of America," Sanders said.

Sen John Fetterman Pledges To Be 'Last Man Standing' In The Democratic Party In Support Of Israel

Sanders appeared to be referencing a July Quinnipiac University survey that found 19% of Pennsylvania Democrats approved of Fetterman's job performance, while 69% disapproved. The same survey found that 77% of Republicans approved of Fetterman, although his overall approval rating among registered voters was 48%.

When reached for comment on Sanders' Sunday commentary, Fetterman's office pointed Fox News Digital to remarks he shared with Semafor on Thursday in which he intensified his criticism of Sanders over the collapse of Platner's campaign. The Pennsylvania Democrat accused Sanders of promoting Platner amid multiple controversies and scandals before the former candidate withdrew from Maine's Senate race.

"You were the carnival barker for an accused rapist. You should have taken my advice, since you and P-Hustle blew up the Maine race," Fetterman said. "Take responsibility and apologize."

Fetterman Brands New Socialist Favorite 'Pontiac Platner' After 'Ogre' Dig

"After you just blasted the Maine race apart, you are in Michigan replicating it," Fetterman said, referring to Sanders' support of progressive Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

The clash followed months of tension between the senators over Platner and the Democratic Party's approach to Israel.

"Meet the Press" host Kristen Welker played a clip in which Fetterman accused Sanders of helping elevate Platner despite controversies surrounding the former candidate.

"I would be frustrated with someone like Bernie Sanders," Fetterman said. "You know, why, why aren't people angry why they promoted, you know, someone like Platner, an accused rapist."

"So really, Bernie, you have no regret endorsing and proud to stand with an accused rapist, a guy that roughs-up his ex-girlfriends, a guy that had a Nazi tattoo on his chest."

John Fetterman Erupts Over 'Creeper' Graham Platner, Suggesting He's A 'Nazi Sympathizer'

Fetterman previously demanded that Sanders apologize to Maine voters and everyone who donated to Platner's campaign.

Sanders later called for Platner to leave the race after a former girlfriend accused him of rape, an allegation Platner denied.

Welker asked Sanders whether he regretted endorsing Platner before the allegation emerged. Sanders defended the campaign Platner ran, while acknowledging the seriousness of the accusation that prompted his withdrawal.

"Well, you know, it's easy to be a Monday morning quarterback," Sanders said. "Platner ran a very strong campaign and, in fact, many of the issues that he's raised are resonating all over this country. A woman made very serious allegations against him, he withdrew from the race, period."

title: Trump frequently announces he's halting strikes in Iran. But they keep happening
description: President Donald Trump said late Saturday that he would halt new planned attacks on Iran pending renewed talks to wind down the war and revive stalled cargo traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.  It w...
fullText:
TEL AVIV, Israel (AP) — President Donald Trump said late Saturday that he would halt new planned attacks on Iran pending renewed talks to wind down the war and revive stalled cargo traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

It was the latest in a pattern of announcements the U.S. president has made to first threaten massive strikes and then later call them off. The abrupt shifts have been a defining feature of the five-month conflict that has sent prices of oil and basic goods soaring — and the announcements to date have been upended by renewed attacks days or even hours afterward.

Here is a look at some of Trump's past major announcements about pausing strikes against Iran:

The United States and Iran agree to a two-week ceasefire to end the intense fighting that began on Feb. 28 with Israeli and U.S. attacks. Trump makes the announcement less than two hours before a deadline he had set for Tehran to capitulate or face attacks on bridges and power plants — strikes he said would mean "a whole civilization will die."

Trump announces that the U.S. is indefinitely extending its ceasefire with Iran a day before it was to expire. He adds that he has been asked by mediators to hold off on attacks to give Iranian leaders time to come up with additional proposals. The fragile ceasefire lasts until May 8, when the U.S. carried out strikes on Iranian tankers.

After a weekend of dire threats against Iran, Trump says he is holding off on a major planned military strike because "serious negotiations" were underway. "There seems to be a very good chance that they can work something out. If we can do that without bombing the hell out of them, I'd be very happy," he said. By May 27, U.S. strikes were back on after negotiations faltered.

After two days of back-and-forth attacks, Trump threatens further escalation, saying the U.S. would hit Iran "VERY HARD TONIGHT" and take "total control" of its oil and gas industries. Then, a few hours later, Trump posts on social media that there had been a breakthrough in negotiations and called off the strikes.

Trump signs an initial agreement with Iran that calls for a permanent end to hostilities and for reopening of the strait, and starts a 60-day negotiating clock to reach a final deal on the future of Iran's nuclear program. Trump left the door open to abandoning it. "It's a memorandum of understanding, and if I don't like it, we'll go back to shooting at them, dropping bombs," he said.

After Iranian attacks on commercial ships in the strait, Trump launches new strikes on Iran while he is in Ankara, Turkey, attending the NATO leaders' summit. Later, he renews his threat to "just finish the job" on Iran after saying he believes the ceasefire is over.

Trump says he has paused two weeks of intense, daily U.S. strikes on Iran to give negotiations another chance. During 13 days of strikes, the U.S. military had targeted key military and commercial sites as clashes continued to escalate over shipping routes. In response, Iran had launched missiles and drones across the Middle East at countries that host U.S. troops.

After telling reporters the U.S. would hit Iran "very hard," Trump says on social media that he has canceled planned strikes, claiming Mideast allies had reached the parameters of a deal to end the war, including a reopening of the strait. "Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," Trump said. In response, Iran's defense minister said that the country was "neither surprised nor passive" following Trump's announcement and said Iran continues to remain alert in the face of threats.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is facing a conservative backlash after reaffirming his opposition to amnesty in a social media post, with critics arguing the hardline message contradicted comments he made hours earlier during an immigration speech in Oklahoma.

Hours after speaking at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting in Oklahoma City, Mullin wrote on X: "NO amnesty for illegal aliens. Ever."

"We are a nation of laws," he wrote. "If you are illegally present in the United States of America—you will be detained and deported. Period."

The post did little to quell criticism from some conservatives, who argued it conflicted with remarks Mullin made earlier in the day.

Red State Governor Pummeled Online After Defying Trump's Deportation Orders

"Why were you at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting today saying the exact opposite of what you are posting now?" one user wrote on X. "Did you suddenly radically change your mind about America's immigration policy in the past couple of hours? Or are you a liar?"

Former Border Patrol Chief Gregory Bovino also criticized Mullin's remarks, writing on X that "Voters asked for mass deportations. Clear demand. High priority. No ambiguity." He added, "The guy running DHS is making the case for 'immigration reform.' We've seen this script before."

In a separate post, Bovino wrote that Mullin had delivered "a masterclass in how to give terrible answers during a single interview" and argued, "Now you know why we're not getting mass deportations."

Conservative commentator Robby Starbuck also weighed in, calling Mullin's remarks "a total betrayal."

During the event, Mullin argued the U.S. needs immigration reform, distinguished between immigrants pursuing legal status and those who are not, and called for changes to some employment visa programs to address labor shortages.

"We haven't had actual immigration reform since 1959. There's a reason. It's political," Mullin said. "Do you really need immigration reform? Yes, you do."

Biden Administration Forced A False Choice On Americans About Immigration

Mullin also argued the country should modernize some employment visa programs.

"If we're looking to grow our economy, then we need to look at making more permanent solutions," he said, adding that "there's a way to utilize labor where we're not having the participation rate we need to... and we can plug those holes."

At the same time, Mullin repeatedly emphasized that immigration laws must be enforced.

"If you have a criminal background, we're not making exceptions for you," he said. "There are zero exceptions."

Mullin added that immigrants who entered the country illegally or overstayed their visas without pursuing legal status could not expect relief.

"There's nothing I can do for you," he said.

The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

fullText:
TOKYO, Aug 2 (Reuters) - Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama will announce on Monday that Tokyo and Washington took joint action in the currency market to arrest the yen's slide to 40-year lows, two Japanese government officials told Reuters.

Katayama is likely ‌to stress the two countries' determination to combat what they consider excessive yen declines, said the sources familiar with the matter, on condition of ‌anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue.

One source, asked if Katayama would announce "joint action", said yes, adding, "The operation is still ongoing."

The Ministry of Finance could not immediately be reached for comment on ​Sunday. U.S. Treasury Department officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

FIRST JOINT YEN INTERVENTION IN 15 YEARS

The expected announcement follows what market sources say were rounds of yen-buying in the market by the Japanese and U.S. authorities, the first joint intervention since 2011, seeking to boost the Japanese currency from its lowest levels against the dollar since 1986.

The Japanese government bought yen for dollars in New York trading hours on Thursday, a market source told Reuters, with Bank of Japan data suggesting it sold as ‌much as $58.97 billion to support the yen.

Tokyo's initial intervention came ⁠hours before the BOJ decided on Friday to keep monetary policy steady while signalling a strong chance it would raise interest rates soon. A widening rate differential with the U.S., where the Federal Reserve has dramatically shifted to a more hawkish stance, has ⁠been a key factor in the dollar's rise against the yen.

Shortly after BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda held a press conference on the central bank's decision, the yen spiked in what markets suspect may have been another bout of yen-buying intervention by Tokyo.

"Going forward, as the official responsible for currency policy, I would like to respond in close coordination with monetary ​policy," ​Katayama's top currency diplomat, Atsushi Mimura, told reporters after the yen's spike on Friday, suggesting the ​MOF and BOJ were working hand in hand to combat ‌the weak yen.

Also on Friday, the U.S. Treasury informed a number of banks that it might intervene in the yen market and that they should "stand ready for future action", a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who said last week the yen "seems very undervalued to me", had a notepad at a Friday cabinet meeting with the words "To Do", followed by "Buy Japanese Yen (JPY) $5-10 bil", a Reuters photo showed.

title: What smart people are saying about Trump Media charging for early access to the president's Truth Social posts
description: Trump Media launched Truth API on Saturday, allowing early access to posts from prominent Truth Social accounts, including President Donald Trump's.
fullText:
Trump Media launched Truth API on Saturday.

Truth API sells early access to posts from prominent Truth Social users like President Donald Trump.

There's a new way to make and lose money.

Trump Media has officially launched the Truth API, a business-to-business data feed that provides customers with faster access to posts from prominent Truth Social accounts. That includes President Donald Trump, whose constant stream of posts can cause shifts in financial markets.

Institutional customers gained access to the service on Saturday. A few hours later, Trump announced on Truth Social that he was, again, close to a deal to end his war on Iran. On any other day, that post would have affected oil futures, and anyone with early access could have made a buck.

"Markets already move on Truth Social posts," Kevin McGurn, interim CEO of Trump Media, said in a press release. "Truth API delivers a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform's most market-moving Truths while advancing our strategy to monetize proprietary assets through a high-margin, recurring revenue stream."

Trump Media has not publicly disclosed how much the service is costing customers. Reuters reported that the company discussed charging up to $100,000 a month, or $60,000 a month as part of a three-year plan.

The whole thing got people talking.

Here's what smart people in finance, academia, and policy are saying about Truth API.

Jim Bianco, the president of Bianco Research, a market analysis firm, said in a post on X that Truth API could result in "more frequent market-moving posts" on the social media site.

"Trump will want them to be happy with their new service," Bianco wrote on Saturday, referring to Truth API customers.

Shaun Maguire, a venture capitalist and partner at Sequoia Capital who is a vocal supporter of Trump, said he isn't a fan of the service in an X post on Sunday.

"Moves like this cheapen Trump's policy wins (of which there have been many)," Maguire said.

Dean Baker, cofounder of the Center for Economic and Policy Research, said the service may work at the expense of everyday Americans.

"And, since reporters are too lazy to tell people, the money that insider traders pocket is money taken from the 401(k)s and IRAs of normal people who work for a living," Baker said in an X post on Saturday.

On Sunday, finance journalist and author James Surowiecki said he believes Truth API violates insider trading laws.

title: Superbug confirmed in 23 states: Where is the deadly fungus spreading in 2026?
description: The drug-resistant and deadly fungus Candida auris has proven hard to stamp out in 2026. Despite efforts to contain its spread, the fungus is once again on the move, new data from the Centers for Dise...
fullText:
(NEXSTAR) – The drug-resistant and deadly fungus Candida auris has proven hard to stamp out in 2026. Despite efforts to contain its spread, the fungus is once again on the move, new data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows.

Candida auris was first reported in the U.S. in 2016 and has spread rapidly over the past several years. Some strains of the fungus are considered a superbug because they're resistant to all types of medications usually used to treat fungal infections.

While healthy people may be able to fight off the infection on their own, the fungus can be deadly in health care settings, where people are often sick and vulnerable. Candida auris can survive on surfaces for long periods of time before spreading to patients through catheters, breathing tubes or IVs.

So far in 2026, nearly half of U.S. states have reported cases to the CDC. The most cases are in Texas, which had more than 700 known cases as of mid-July.

Michigan, the current epicenter of a very different public health outbreak, is close behind with 503 cases of Candida auris.

See which states are reporting the most cases of Candida auris in the map below.

A recent review of the fungus' spread between 2022 and 2024 found that the vast majority of clinical cases, about 88%, were in people over the age of 45. A majority of patients were men and most were in acute care settings.

When it spreads in a health care setting, where patients' health is already compromised, the fungus can be deadly.

"If you get infected with this pathogen that's resistant to any treatment, there's no treatment we can give you to help combat it. You're all on your own," Melissa Nolan, an assistant professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at the University of South Carolina, previously told Nexstar.

In the past, the CDC estimated that "based on information from a limited number of patients, 30–60% of people with C. auris infections have died. However, many of these people had other serious illnesses that also increased their risk of death."

title: Iran's leaders show a united front over the war but are divided over what the goal is
description: With escalating attacks against U.S. bases and its allies over the past week, Iran's leaders are showing considerable unity over their war strategy: hanging tough, determined to show Iran can endure m...
fullText:
CAIRO (AP) — With escalating attacks against U.S. bases and its allies over the past week, Iran's leaders are showing considerable unity over their war strategy: hanging tough, determined to show Iran can endure more than America and its allies can.

But within the leadership, there are sharp differences over what the endgame should be.

On one side, the ultra-hardliners who oppose any negotiations with the United States are pressing for total victory in the war. Known as the "Paydari" movement – Persian for "stability" – they are hard-core ideologues who want to enforce the Islamic Republic's control over society.

On the other, those who support President Masoud Pezeshkian and powerful parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf — who doubles as Iran's chief negotiator — see military pressure as a way to win a negotiated deal with the United States. This camp is also spurred by concern over the economic toll Iran is suffering from the war and the need to adapt to social change in the country.

"Negotiation is a political tool and a complement to military action to force the enemy to a point of compulsion and extract real concessions," an adviser to Qalibaf, Mahdi Mohammadi, wrote on his Telegram channel Thursday.

The unusually open rivalry within the theocracy's leadership points to a struggle for control over Iran's postwar future. A huge question mark is where the new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, stands. Reportedly injured in the strike that killed his father in the opening minutes of the war on Feb. 28, Khamenei remains in hiding, and both sides have claimed his support.

In a boost for Qalibaf and Pezeshkian, the ceasefire deal reached with the U.S. in April received strong backing in Iran's top leadership body, the Supreme National Security Council. Twelve of its 13 members approved it, including senior figures in the Revolutionary Guard and the military.

The lone vote against the deal is widely believed to have come from Saeed Jalili, the most prominent figure in the Paydari movement.

But the ceasefire crumbled as the two sides trade strikes and as Iran presses for control over passage through the Strait of Hormuz which before the war carried a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas. Iran was also frustrated that financial promises under the deal – including the release of billions of frozen assets – didn't materialize, and now the American blockade is back in place.

With no benefits from the deal, "there's no serious division" in the leadership over how to respond, said Ali Vaez, Iran project director at the International Crisis Group.

They believe U.S. President Donald Trump "only understands the language of force, and therefore, they would have to gain the upper hand in order to compel him to deliver," Vaez said.

The funeral for slain Iranian supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, earlier this month appeared to show the strength of the ultra-hardline Paydari. Crowds called for revenge on the U.S. and Israel for the war. Videos showed mourners in Tehran welcoming Jalili, while Pezeshkian was greeted at one point with insults and cries of "Death to the compromiser!".

The ultra-hardliners have used nightly rallies and their control of state television, known by the acronym IRIB, to drum up opposition to negotiations. At rallies and on TV, speakers have portrayed Iran as headed for total victory and denounced those who compromise with the Islamic Republic's archenemy, the United States.

State television cut off a June 30 live broadcast with Qalibaf as he discussed negotiations with Washington. Earlier this month, it cut off broadcasting a speech by Pezeshkian to businessmen seconds after he said that the elder Khamenei had given permission for renewed U.S. talks before his death.

Pezeshkian and his camp have pushed back, portraying IRIB as dividing the country at the time of war. The president accused the broadcaster of making it like "the military are on one side, and the government is on another side."

Last month, the president's media office condemned state television for what it described as "censoring" the president and other government heads, signaling an open rift.

The hard-liners have sought to press their influence in other ways. In past weeks, authorities shut down cafes in central Tehran that were popular with residents during the ceasefire. Videos on Iranian social media showed many women at the cafes flouting mandatory veiling laws, and crowds mixing freely.

The closures were brief but signaled that "religious extremist parties" were showing their influence, said Mohamad Ali Abtahi, a reformist cleric and an aide to former President Mohammad Khatami, who is still widely considered to be the leader of Iran's reformist groups.

While Jalili's supporters are a minority they are influential, said Vali Nasr, professor of International Affairs and Middle East Studies at Johns Hopkins University.

"They have a lot of money. They have a lot of power. They have put a lot of people in the bureaucracy" and developed connections in the Revolutionary Guard, Nasr said.

The more pragmatic camp argues that maintaining unity during the war requires addressing the public's unhappiness over the economy as well as political and social repression. This, as Iran's currency continues to slide, inflation spirals, and unemployment rises. A final agreement with the U.S. could bring Iran a huge windfall with the lifting of sanctions and the return of billions in assets.

Small flashes of impatience with the war have emerged. In July, over 250 former lawmakers, clerics, professors and other public figures signed an anti-war petition warning of the costs of the conflict. "We believe that the overwhelming majority of the Iranian people want peace and the right to a decent life," the statement read. Others have spoken out against stepped-up executions of protesters following wide-scale anti-government protests in January.

A top reformist party that assisted Pezeshkian's presidential campaign warned that the war's domestic toll was "undermining internal social cohesion." That brought a rebuke from Tasnim, a news agency close to the Revolutionary Guard, which said the statement amounted to blaming Iran for a war started by the United States.

In mid-July, the president's son and influential adviser, Youssef Pezeshkian, posted a series of messages about the need to balance realistic military aims with a weak economy. Referring to the decades of sanctions and confrontation with the West, he said Iran has "been prevented from growing and has suffered greatly. It has become sick."

Ultimately, both sides are jockeying for power after the war, given the unusual uncertainty brought on by the change in the supreme leadership. Abtahi, the reformist cleric, said Mojtaba Khamenei's real views are still not known, so while some believe he could be more radical than his father, others see the potential for him to bring moderate change.

The supreme leader, because of the power invested in him, could act as a "brake" to restrain the more extremist factions, Abtahi said. But over time, the confrontation with more radical factions could grow more dangerous "if that brake isn't used."

AP correspondents Nasser Karimi in Tehran and Sarah El Deeb in Beirut contributed to this report.

title: GOP senator on Trump’s Reflecting Pool vandalism claims: ‘He grows anxious when he has an unexpressed thought’
description: Republican Sen. John Kennedy (La.) said Sunday he is unsure whether President Trump truly believes his claims that vandals damaged the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. “I don’t know whether he really...
fullText:
Republican Sen. John Kennedy (La.) said Sunday he is unsure whether President Trump truly believes his claims that vandals damaged the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

"I don't know whether he really believes that, or it's part of his political messaging, or he's just thinking out loud," Kennedy told host Kristen Welker on NBC News's "Meet the Press."

"You and I both know the president well," the Louisiana Republican added. "He exists loudly, and he grows anxious when he has an unexpressed thought. I'm not saying he doesn't really believe it, I just don't know."

The Justice Department moved Friday to drop its criminal prosecution of Olympian David Hearn over allegations he damaged the Reflecting Pool

In a 20-page filing, the Justice Department pinned the damage to the site on a "rushed and botched installation" Atlantic Industrial Coatings carried out this spring and summer to repaint the bottom of the pool. The department also faulted the Interior Department for a "barebones" report about the incident involving Hearn.

"Specifically, the newly released documents reveal that work on installing the lining almost immediately fell behind, due to a combination of very rainy and windy weather, repeated failures of testing on the sealing of the expansion joints, and delays in obtaining sealing product at the worksite," wrote prosecutors from the office of U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who oversees Washington, D.C.

"The rush to complete the project led to hasty and botched work that was not remediated before the project was finished and the fencing removed," prosecutors added.

Associate Judge Todd Edelman, an appointee of former President Obama who sits on the District of Columbia's Superior Court, has the final say on whether to dismiss the case against Hearn — a three-time Olympic canoeist who pleaded not guilty to felony destruction of property last month.

Trump said he disagreed "100%" with Pirro's decision to drop the case. The president appointed Pirro — a former local prosecutor, judge and Fox News host — to her post in May 2025.

"I don't know what she was thinking?" the president wrote on Truth Social, referring to Pirro. "To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM. … There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!"

But Kennedy, a lawyer and member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, said Pirro was "smart" to dismiss the prosecution of Hearn, which he called a "multiple vehicle pileup."

"Federal judges will not tolerate," the GOP lawmaker told Welker on Sunday. "And so, I don't know why she filed the suit without doing a full investigation. She says she relied on the Department of Interior. But she was smart to pull it back."

title: As Trump balks again at escalating war, Iran smells ‘blood in the water’ and looks to exploit its newfound strategic advantage, experts say
description: "Last night's events underscore a reality that is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: for now, Iran appears to hold the strategic advantage in deterrence."
fullText:
In what has become a familiar pattern in the Iran war, President Donald Trump again threatened a massive attack then pulled back from the brink.

But while he attributed his latest reversal to U.S. allies pleading with him to give diplomacy another chance, experts also see signs Iran is gaining the upper hand.

That's as Tehran has used its proxies to expand the war across the region, most notably Houthis rebels threatening ships in the Red Sea that are trying to use the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

At the same time, Iran has warned its Persian Gulf neighbors they will be targets in the event of a renewed bombardment after demonstrating that its long-range weapons can evade U.S. air defenses.

"Iran and its clients see blood in the water and see a benefit for all of them in escalating and entering the fray," Afshon Ostovar, an Iran expert at the Naval Postgraduate School, told the Financial Times.

He added that their goal is to prolong the conflict instead of inflicting more severe damage as Iran looks to exploit less political endurance on the other side.

"So the longer it continues, the weaker the resolve of their enemies will be," Ostovar explained. "That is how they see it."

Indeed, Trump's approval ratings on his handling of the economy have slumped alongside his numbers on the Iran war, with support slipping even among Republicans.

And now that midterm elections are just a few months away and gas prices are back up again, Tehran sees leverage in the U.S. political calendar.

An Iranian diplomat told the Wall Street Journal that the regime is prepared to take advantage of Trump political vulnerability and would consider preemptive strikes if talks fail.

That aggressive stance was on display last week, when Iran launched unprovoked attacks on U.S. bases in what Central Command called an "attempted surprise attack."

To be sure, the U.S. still retains significant military assets in the region and continues to enforce a naval blockade on Iran that's causing more economic pain.

But the U.S. and its allies have also severely depleted stockpiles of interceptors needed to repel Iranian attacks, making critical pieces of their energy infrastructure more at risk.

Global energy markets have also sharply drawn down inventories of crude oil and refined products, with analysts warning that "tank bottoms" will be just around the corner unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens soon.

The combined effect is that the overall playing field has tilted in favor of the Islamic Republic.

"Last night's events underscore a reality that is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: for now, Iran appears to hold the strategic advantage in deterrence," Dennis Citrinowicz, a former Israeli intelligence official who specialized in Iran, posted on X. "It has succeeded in creating a form of mutual deterrence that is shaping Washington's calculations."

Despite suffering heavy losses at that start of the war, Iran has since shown it can hold the global economy hostage by threatening maritime chokepoints and its Gulf neighbors, he added.

In fact, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke directly with Trump on Saturday to express concern over the plans for massive new U.S. strikes on Iran, sources told Axios.

The kingdom's de facto ruler reportedly urged Trump to de-escalate and refrain from launching the attacks, days after the Saudi defense minister conveyed a similar message.

"President Trump may still decide to order military action. But the fact that Washington continues to hesitate suggests that it recognizes the risks of escalation and is not convinced that a broader campaign would compel Iran to back down," Citrinowicz wrote.

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

title: Bournemouth close in on £11.1m Juanlu
description: Bournemouth are finalising an £11.1m move for Sevilla right-back Juanlu as new manager Marco Rose's squad nears completion.
fullText:
Bournemouth are finalising an £11.1m move for Sevilla right-back Juanlu as new manager Marco Rose's squad nears completion.

The 22-year-old will cost an initial £9.4m, with a further £1.7m in add-ons, and is expected to move to the south coast on a long-term contract.

Juanlu is a tall, attacking full-back with significant experience despite his young age and has been heavily capped at Spanish youth level.

It would be the Cherries' third signing of the summer after the arrivals of Antonio Silva from Benfica for £25.7m and striker Alvaro Rodriguez from Elche - also for £25.7m - earlier in the transfer window.

Rose is now looking only for a number two goalkeeper capable of challenging Djordje Petrovic as Bournemouth continue pre-season before a historic campaign in which they will compete in the Europa League for the first time.

Sevilla have shown an interest in striker Enes Unal, whom Bournemouth are keen to sell. However, the Turkey international also has options in Turkey and Saudi Arabia as he looks to secure a move this summer.

Star trio Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan and Alex Scott remain unavailable for sale, according to senior sources at the Vitality Stadium.

title: How Johansson is rising to daunting Motherwell challenge
description: With significant departures on and off the field, new Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson appeared to have a daunting task on his hands this season, but he has started in fine style.
fullText:
Sportscene highlights: Hibernian 1-2 Motherwell

Alfred Johansson appeared to have walked into an incredibly difficult job at Motherwell this summer.

Motherwell finished fourth in the Scottish Premiership last season, playing some of the best football you could wish to see, and all on one of the top-flight's lowest budgets.

Not only was Johansson following in Jens Berthel Askou's sizeable footsteps after the Danish manager left for Toulouse, he was also dealing with the departures of key players in Elijah Just, Elliot Watt and Calum Ward, who have joined Swansea City, Samsunspor and QPR, respectively.

And yet, the Swede has started in fine style.

Sunday's 2-1 win at Hibernian was a third victory on the spin after a 5-0 aggregate success against Faroese outfit HB Torshavn and they showed two very different sides of themselves at Easter Road.

Amid a second-half onslaught from the hosts, Motherwell stood firm, led defensively by summer recruit Martin Moormann, before Ibrahim Said scored a brilliant winner on the break.

"It was a game of ups and downs for both teams and obviously I'm really pleased to come out with the three points," Johansson said.

"In the first half we showed some good stuff on the ball, but more than tactics, we have to praise the spirit of the team because at times we had to ride out storms.

"We have Martin Moormann throwing himself to make blocks, the front three dropping deep to help and Alex Paulsen making exceptional saves.

"When we hit it off, the good periods look really good, but we want those periods to be longer, but even months from now when we are better we will have to suffer and the guys showed they are ready to do that."

Superb Said goal earns Motherwell late win at Hibs

Motherwell's good periods at Easter Road got no better than the decisive goal, as they sliced Hibs open with slick one-touch passing.

Alex Lowry played a neat one-two with Said, released Dylan Williams down the left and he squared it to the Nigerian attacking midfielder, who slotted into the bottom corner and wheeled away towards a jubilant away end.

Johansson has continued to play a similar possession-based style to Askou, implementing small tweaks rather than significant change.

More than the performance though, it was the mentality of Johansson's side that impressed former St Johnstone and Queen's Park manager Callum Davidson.

"Hibs were the better team in the second half, but then Motherwell get the goal on the counter-attack," he said on BBC Sportsound.

"Hibs will be so disappointed in how they lose the second goal. Motherwell took their chances and defended really well. It was a gritty display."

Johansson pointed out eight players were making their Motherwell league debuts in Sunday's win - five of them from the start.

"To show that kind of commitment and team spirit this early, all the credit to the players. It shows we have got the right characters in the door," the Motherwell boss said.

The recruitment done so far certainly appears to be astute, with Moormann and fellow centre-back Jake Girdwood-Reich particularly impressive.

Those new players have plugged the gaps left, while combining with proven performers like Said and academy talents such as Mikey Booth, who started both legs against HB.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, given the fast start to the new season, Motherwell are clearly enjoying these early weeks under the 35-year-old.

"The group was so together, it still feels the same. It feels like a family," said Regan Charles-Cook before the trip to Easter Road.

"The manager has brought in his own methods and stamped his authority on the team. We're all really enjoying it," midfielder Oscar Priestman told Sky Sports.

Yes, sterner games are still to come - starting at HJK Helsinki in the third qualifying round of the Conference League on Thursday - but Johansson and his new-look side have passed every test to date with flying colours.

title: What could full season of O'Neill at Celtic look like?
description: Martin O'Neill has vowed to "drive forward together" and "not rest on past success", so what could a full season with the Northern Irishman at the helm look like?
fullText:
Scottish Premiership: Celtic v Dundee

Listen to live match commentary of Celtic's opening match of the new Scottish Premiership season on BBC Sounds and watch highlights on the BBC iPlayer.

Celtic were about 10 minutes away from losing their Scottish Premiership crown. What that would have meant for Martin O'Neill's future is unclear.

Instead, a late winner from Daizen Maeda and a chaotic title-sealing goal from Callum Osmand claimed the trophy they have dominated in an unforgettable final-day decider against Hearts.

A Scottish Cup triumph followed the next weekend, before O'Neill was confirmed as permanent boss after a tumultuous season in which the 74-year-old had two interim stints at the club where he holds legendary status.

Despite a memorable end to the campaign, a lack of transfer business was again threatening to become the story of another summer at Celtic.

However, the arrival of striker Kasper Hogh for a club-record fee, coupled with a positive pre-season for fellow new attacker Camilo Duran, has somewhat eased the restlessness within the fanbase.

O'Neill has vowed to "drive forward together" and "not rest on past success", so what could a full season with the Northern Irishman at the helm look like?

Celtic reject Engels bid and confirm Johnston interest

Celtic 'a really good match' for record signing Kogh

Ipswich sign Japan forward Maeda from Celtic

The 82 points Celtic finished with last term was the lowest for a champion across a full Premiership season since Celtic themselves hit the same tally in an uncompetitive 2017-18 campaign at the summit.

O'Neill's side were responsible for 59 of those points across 23 league games in charge over his two spells.

That averages out at about 2.6 points per game. Spread that over a 38-game season and you get a staggering final tally of 99, which resembles O'Neill's league-winning totals in the early 2000s.

Across his full seasons in charge in his first spell two decades ago, he recorded tallies of 97, 103, 97, 98 and 92, winning the title in three of those campaigns.

He also went unbeaten in cup competitions last term, taking the team to a League Cup final, which they lost under Wilfried Nancy, before winning the Scottish Cup in his second interim stint.

Had Celtic opted against hiring Nancy and kept O'Neill in charge for the remainder of the 2025-26 season, it is very possible they would have finished the campaign with another domestic treble and a greater cushion at the top of the league table.

Given the desperate state of Celtic's season in January, O'Neill's return after Nancy's exit was a case of getting by and staying in touch with the leaders.

Results took priority as the team attempted to string wins together to claw back the deficit at the summit.

However, after a full pre-season, fans will be expecting 

Shaun Maloney, Mark Fotheringham and Stephen McManus will again form part of O'Neill's backroom staff.

O'Neill is not one to do much on-field training and trusts his coaches to handle many of those duties, but he has stressed he wants his team to be flexible, and has hinted at deploying Kogh and Duran together up front in a departure from Celtic's favoured 4-3-3 formation.

Former Hertha Berlin assistant Fotheringham is inspired by high-intensity German football, while ex-Hibernian manager Maloney is known to be something of a football purist.

It will be intriguing to see how that dynamic works after a summer's worth of work, while the addition of set-piece specialist Ross Grant from Hearts highlights how Celtic are looking to place greater emphasis on their dead-ball output.

Despite ending the season with a league and cup double, the concern for Celtic fans was that an ultimately successful campaign would mean the club's decision-makers learn nothing from the reasons that made the year a rollercoaster.

Recruitment has regularly been scrutinised, with the past two transfer windows unconvincing at best.

Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren represent the only two players among 17 incomings across the past 12 months who will go into next season as recognised starters.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain penned an extension after playing a part in the second half of last term before the arrival of Duran from Qarabag.

The exit of Daizen Maeda, last season's title hero, following confirmation that Kelechi Iheanacho and Marcelo Saracchi would not be returning to Parkhead, cranked up the fury among the fanbase.

But do the arrivals of Duran and Hogh point towards a quality-over-quantity approach?

The attacking pair have come with a reported combined cost of about £15m and arrive with Champions League pedigree.

Duran has impressed in pre-season after scoring five of his 15 goals for Qarabag last term in Uefa's premier club competition. Hogh netted the same number in the same tournament as Bodo/Glimt defied the odds to reach the last 16.

Little business had been done by the time Celtic were dumped out of Champions League qualifying by Kairat Almaty last year, setting the tone for Brendan Rodgers' ugly exit.

Principal shareholder Dermot Desmond has insisted the club would ensure they are well prepared for the upcoming season. That was echoed by interim chairman Brian Wilson and chief executive Michael Nicholson.

Fans are yet to be totally convinced by that given only two new faces have been recruited, but both arrive with CVs showing they can deliver at the highest level.

It is imperative that the board deliver on their promise after mounting unrest between fans and club threatened to somewhat derail last season.

It also cannot be taken for granted that O'Neill has now shown he can lead Celtic to honours with a squad light on both numbers and quality. He too will be demanding that the squad is strengthened.

Failure to do so would only risk a repeat of last year's humiliation against Kairat and, therefore, their place at Europe's top table.

It was Europa League football for Celtic last term, with elimination to Stuttgart in the first knockout round after a 4-1 home defeat was followed by a 1-0 win in Germany.

Although it counted for nothing in terms of progression, that away victory in Stuttgart reaffirmed O'Neill's European credentials - as did an earlier win at Feyenoord and a draw at Bologna with 10 men.

However, the tracksuit-wearing veteran will want to be doing his dugout air jumps in Uefa's premier club competition this season.

No Champions League money for a second campaign running could severely impact summer spending towards the end of the window.

Plus, with Maeda gone and Arne Engels linked with a move away, the lure of top-level European football can prove crucial in persuading star players to stay.

It has been more than 20 years since O'Neill managed a Champions League match, or even a qualifier. A two-time European Cup winner with Nottingham Forest, his record as a manager in the competition stands at six wins from 18 matches.

In three qualification attempts for the Champions League, he has been successful twice. There was also a Uefa Cup final appearance in 2003 and he made it to the quarters the following year.

A two-legged play-off, set for 18-19 August and 25-26 August, stands between an older and wiser O'Neill and a return to the pinnacle of club football, where he could flex that European pedigree.

Before then, an intriguing Premiership defence starts with a Monday night encounter at home to Dundee on 3 August and a trip to Kilmarnock the following Sunday.

title: Game of the season in Premiership's opening weekend?
description: Newly-promoted St Johnstone block out summer "noise" to thrill fans with a goal-laden win over Kilmarnock on the Premiership opening weekend.
fullText:
Sportscene highlights: St Johnstone 4-3 Kilmarnock

"I cannot see this St Johnstone team doing much."

That was the statement made by Sky Sports pundit Kris Boyd before kick-off in Sunday's season opener for the Perth club and Kilmarnock.

In fairness to the former Killie striker, no one expected what was to come.

Ninety breathless minutes of football later, seven goals had been scored, the lead had changed hands twice and crucially, Simo Valakari's side had all three points.

Was it a surprise? They were Scottish Championship winners at a canter, while Kilmarnock only scored twice in the League Cup group stage.

However, Neil McCann's men also kept four clean sheets while the Saints had crashed out after a loss to Inverness and a draw with East Fife.

So just how did these two sides produce what BBC Sportsound pundit Allan Preston hailed as "an early contender for game of the season"?

St Johnstone edge out Kilmarnock in seven-goal epic

Podcast: Reaction as St Johnstone and Motherwell start with wins

Memories are short in football. Last season Valakari led his side to an immediate top-flight return, scoring 14 goals more than any other Championship team. Of the five top scorers in the league, three belonged to St Johnstone.

But there was an indication pre-match the Finn would modify his style. "How we played last year was the best way to win the Championship... we do not want to be a naive, romantic team who plays nice football and loses matches," he told BBC Scotland. "We need to be solid and streetwise."

And after their League Cup exit, St Johnstone fans had concerns heading into the league campaign.

There's been eight summer signings, three of whom were previous loans turned permanent, and some frustration that Valakari hasn't been busier.

Yet from the off against Kilmarnock, St Johnstone hunted in packs and poured forward - mainly down the left where Ruari Paton and Jamie Gullan combined.

It was that pair who linked up to cut back for Josh Fowler, the striker opening the scoring with a Premiership goal just four years after playing for Beith Juniors.

Saints were on top for much of the game, but were twice pegged back and then somehow found themselves 3-2 down. Their response was helped by a manager who chucked on three attacking subs and hooked his central midfielders as soon as they went behind.

Such boldness was rewarded with a Jason Holt own goal and Kai Fotheringham's fiecely-struck winner.

All that speaks to a side used to fighting tooth and nail for all three points and getting their own way. Perhaps that's why Valakari has trusted in those who got them back to the Premiership promised land.

"I know there has a been a lot of talk, outside noise, where we are with [the squad]," said Valakri.

"We are not getting carried away, we know where we are and what we need to improve. There might be some suffering in front of us."

McCann and his assistant Billy Dodds were praised last season for turning around a sinking Kilmarnock ship and keeping them afloat.

If this showing is anything to go by, they're facing a similarly difficult task.

Scoring was never an issue last season. They were the top scorers in the bottom half. It was at the back they were shaky - only Livingston conceded more - and that haunted them again in Perth.

Yes, they did well to come from behind to lead. But St Johnstone only created 1.76 xG and still managed to score four goals. They were not particularly clinical either, having 15 efforts on goal.

The reality is the goals were soft, in particular the second that Cheick Diabate scored from a corner.

All this combines to a fantastic game for the neutral. "It was breathtaking, to be honest," said Preston on Sportsound.

"If we can better this in the next 37 weeks, we're going to have some season. It was brilliant.

"Kilmarnock were never in it in the first half, and lucky to be level at the break. Then they go ahead, incredibly. All credit to Simo Valakari, he chucks on as many forwards as he's got on the bench.

"They just ground it out and it was a brilliant result. 4-3 flatters Kilmarnock to be honest, they didn't play well at all."

Sometimes managers can save face after such results, dancing around the truth to make it sound closer than it really was. McCann was in no such mood.

"I didn't find it entertaining whatsoever," he said after the game, straight-faced. "We got exactly what we deserved from the game - nothing.

"We let ourselves down, the club down, the fans down."
